Wide receivers coach | highlights = * Third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[2001 College Football All-America Team|2001]]) * First-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] (2001) | statlabel1 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Receptions]] | statvalue1 = 217 | statlabel2 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue2 = 3,749 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 15 }} '''Ashley Jovon Lelie''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ə|ˈ|l|iː}}; born February 16, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).{{cite news | title=Chiefs add free-agent receiver Lelie | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4404150 | work=ESPN.com | agency=Associated Press | date=August 17, 2009 | access-date=August 17, 2009}} He played [[college football]] for the [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football|Hawaii Warriors]] and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the first round of the [[2002 NFL draft]] with the 19th overall pick. Lelie also played for the [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and was briefly signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], but was released before the 2009 season began. ==Early life== Lelie attended [[Radford High School (Honolulu, Hawaii)|Radford High School]] in [[Honolulu, Hawaii]], and was a three-sport standout in football, track, and basketball. In football, he won All-District and All-State honors. In basketball, he won All-District honors and in track, he won an All-League honors. In 2006, Lelie donated a scoreboard to his alma mater. Ashley is the son of retired [[USMC|United States Marine]] Rene Allday Lelie and Annetta Lelie a nurse.{{cite web| url=http://the.honoluluadvertiser.com/article/2005/Jan/12/sp/sp02p.html | title=Lelie Scores Big with Radford High School| publisher=Honolulu Advertiser | date=January 12, 2005}} ==College career== Lelie was a standout wide receiver at the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]] from 1999 to 2001. He places prominently on [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football statistical leaders#Receiving|Rainbow Warriors' career receiving lists]]: * 8th in career receptions ('''194''') * 5th in career receiving yards ('''3,341''') * 4th in career receiving touchdowns ('''32''') ==Professional career== Lelie was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] with their first pick (19th overall) in the 2002 NFL Draft.{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He became a starter in 2004 when he recorded his best year with 54 receptions for 1,084 yards.{{cite web | title=Ashley Lelie's NFL stats | url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-1/Chiefs-Announce-Roster-Moves/906F2DC8-D9AA-4347-9878-B2024342F8D2 | publisher=Kansas City Chiefs | date=September 5, 2009 | access-date=September 5, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611232337/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-1/Chiefs-Announce-Roster-Moves/906F2DC8-D9AA-4347-9878-B2024342F8D2 | archive-date=June 11, 2011 | url-status=dead }} Lelie became unhappy in Denver at the start of the 2006 season when Denver traded for [[Javon Walker]] during the [[2006 NFL draft]]. He skipped training camp and asked to be traded, which led to tension with head coach [[Mike Shanahan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2447698 |title=Shanahan growing tired of Lelie's absences - NFL - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 16, 2006 |access-date=October 30, 2012}} Lelie was traded to the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in a three-way deal with the [[Washington Redskins]] in August 2006, and went on to play as a backup for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and the [[Oakland Raiders]] in subsequent seasons.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2558101 |title=Falcons acquire disgruntled WR Lelie from Broncos - NFL - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=August 23, 2006 |access-date=October 30, 2012}} ==NFL career statistics== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! colspan="2"| Legend |- | style="background:#cfecec; width:3em;"| | Led the league |- | '''Bold''' | Career high |} === Regular season === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- !rowspan="2"| Year !rowspan="2"| Team !colspan="2"| Games !colspan="6"| Receiving |- ! '''Asante Tyrell Samuel Sr.''' (born January 6, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was born in [[Accra, Ghana]] and raised in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[UCF Knights football|UCF Knights]] and was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the fourth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. Samuel also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He led the NFL twice in interceptions, in 2006 and 2009. He is the father of [[Asante Samuel Jr.]], a cornerback who plays for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

==Early life==
Samuel was born in [[Accra, Ghana]], and raised in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], where he attended [[Boyd H. Anderson High School]] in [[Lauderdale Lakes, Florida]]. As a junior [[quarterback]], he threw for 1,800 yards and rushed for 500 yards. As a senior, Samuel concentrated on defense, and earned All-State honors, and finished his senior year with 4 interceptions and 75 tackles.  Samuel also managed kick and punt return duties.<ref name="PaymentDue">{{cite news |first=Jackie |last=MacMullan |title=Payment due |url=http://www.boston.com/sports/football/patriots/articles/2007/01/07/payment_due/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070110122317/http://www.boston.com/sports/football/patriots/articles/2007/01/07/payment_due/ |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=January 7, 2007 |archive-date=January 10, 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Ten minutes before kickoff of Samuel's final high school game, he replaced his team's injured starting quarterback.  He threw two touchdown passes, intercepted two more, rushed for 80 yards, and even worked on special teams returning kicks and punts.<ref name="PaymentDue" />  Samuel decreased his [[40-yard dash]] time from 4.5 seconds during his sophomore year of high school to 4.49 seconds entering the NFL.<ref name="PaymentDue" />

==College career==
Samuel attended the [[University of Central Florida]], majored in business administration, and played for the [[UCF Knights football]] team.  He finished his college career with 127 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] (102 solo, 25 assisted), 8 [[interception]]s, and a school-record 38 [[Pass deflected|passes deflected]] (the previous record was 34 deflections). Samuel also returned 63 [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]]s for 673 [[yard]]s, for an average of 10.7 yards per return.<ref name="College">[http://www.patriots.com/team/index.cfm?ac=playerbio&bio=23745 "College"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929092702/http://www.patriots.com/team/index.cfm?ac=playerbio&bio=23745 |date=September 29, 2007 }} Asante Samuel, Official New England Patriots Biography</ref>

===New England Patriots===
====2003====
The [[New England Patriots]] selected Samuel in the fourth round (120th overall) of the [[2003 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=March 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Patriots orchestrated a trade with the Denver Broncos to ensure the acquisition of Samuel by agreeing to trade their fourth-([[Bryant McNeal|128th overall]]) and fifth-round ([[Ben Claxton|157th overall]]) picks in the 2003 NFL draft in return for the 2003 fourth-round pick (120th overall) from the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Pick Transactions |url=https://www.prosportstransactions.com/football/DraftTrades/Years/2003.htm |access-date=August 29, 2018 |website=prosportstransactions.com}}</ref> He was the 16th cornerback selected and the last of two cornerbacks drafted by the Patriots in 2003, following second-round pick (39th overall) [[Eugene Wilson (American football)|Eugene Wilson ]].

On June 10, 2003, the  Patriots signed Samuel to a four–year, [[United States dollar|$]]1.68 million rookie contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $312,500.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Asante Samuel contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/atlanta-falcons/asante-samuel-3683/ |access-date=August 29, 2018 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, he competed Tyrone Poole to earn the role as the No. 2 starting cornerback following the departure of [[Otis Smith (American football)|Otis Smith]]. Head coach [[Bill Belichick]] named him a backup and listed him as the No. 3 cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starters [[Tyrone Poole]] and [[Ty Law]]. 

On September 7, 2003, Samuel made his professional regular season debut in the [[2003 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots']] season-opener at the [[2003 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] and made one tackle and one pass deflection as they lost 0–31. On September 21, 2003, Samuel recorded two solo tackles, set a season-high with two pass deflections, and returned his first career interception for a touchdown during a 23–16 win against the [[2003 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. He intercepted a pass attempt by [[Vinny Testaverde]] thrown to wide receiver [[Wayne Chrebet]] and returned it 55–yards to score his first career touchdown. In Week 7, Samuel earned his first career start in place of Ty Law, who was inactive due to an ankle injury. He recorded one solo tackle and broke up one pass during a 19–13 overtime victory at the [[2003 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. On November 3, 2003, Samuel made one solo tackle, one pass deflection, and sealed the Patriots' 30–26 victory at the [[2003 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] by intercepting a pass by [[Danny Kanell]] to wide receiver [[Ashley Lelie]] with 19 seconds remaining in the game.<ref>{{cite web| title=New England Patriots at Denver Broncos - November 3rd, 2003| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200311030den.htm |access-date=May 26, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> In Week 13, he set a season-high with eight combined tackles (seven solo) during a 38–34 loss at the [[2003 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. He appeared in all 16 games throughout his rookie season with one start and finished with a total of 34 combined tackles (29 solo), made five pass deflections, two interceptions, and one touchdown.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Career Overview|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 26, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref>

The [[2003 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] finished the [[2003 NFL season]] with a 14–2 record, earning a first-round bye. On January 10, 2004, Samuel appeared in his first career playoff game, but was limited to two solo tackles during a 17–14 win against the [[2003 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in the Divisional Round. On February 1, 2004, Samuel appeared in [[Super Bowl XXXVIII]], as the Patriots defeated the [[2003 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] 32–29, earning Samuel his first [[Super Bowl ring]].

====2004====
Throughout training camp, Samuel competed against Tyrone Poole to be the No. 2 starting cornerback under defensive coordinator [[Romeo Crennel]]. Head coach Bill Belichick named him the primary backup and listed him as the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind returning starters Ty Law and Tyrone Poole.

In Week 6, starting cornerback Tyrone Poole injured his knee during a 30–20 victory against the [[2004 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]]. Samuel was subsequently named as his replacement as the No. 2 starting cornerback entering Week 7. On October 31, 2004, the Patriots' No. 1 starting cornerback, Ty Law, exited in the first quarter of a 20–34 loss at the [[2004 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] after suffering a fracture to his foot. Samuel would start alongside rookie [[Randall Gay]] for the rest of the season, as Ty Law remained inactive for the last eight games (Weeks 10–17).<ref>{{cite web| title=Patriots notebook: Law's foot comes into focus| url=https://www.milforddailynews.com/story/sports/2004/12/21/patriots-notebook-law-s-foot/41179364007/ |access-date=May 26, 2025| website=milforddailynews.com| author=Michael Felger| date=December 20, 2004}}</ref> On November 7, 2004, Samuel recorded one solo tackle before exiting in the first quarter of a 40–22 victory at the [[2004 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]] due to an injury to his arm. He subsequently remained inactive for the Patriots' 29–6 win against the [[2004 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] in Week 10.<ref>{{cite web| title=Key Injuries Don't Stop These Pats| url=https://www.southcoasttoday.com/story/sports/2004/11/11/key-injuries-don-t-stop/50361701007/ |access-date=May 26, 2025| website=SouthCoastToday.com}}</ref> He was sidelined for two games (Weeks 12–13) due to a shoulder injury, but returned before fully recovering. In Week 14, Samuel set a season-high with three pass deflections and had a pick-six after intercepting a pass by [[Carson Palmer]] to wide receiver [[T. J. Houshmandzadeh]] and returning it 34–yards for a touchdown during a 28–35 victory against the [[2004 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. The following week, he set a season-high with six combined tackles (five solo) and had one pass deflection during a 28–29 loss at the [[2004 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] in Week 15. On December 17, 2004, the Patriots officially placed Poole on injured reserve due to his knee injury that required surgery and rendered him inactive.<ref>{{cite web| title=Poole put on injured reserve with knee injury| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=pasquarelli_len&id=1948889 |access-date=May 26, 2025| website=ESPN.com| date=December 18, 2004}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 39 combined tackles (37 solo), made 12 pass deflections, three forced fumbles, one interception, and one touchdown in 13 games and eight starts.<ref name="career"/>

The [[2004 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] finished the [[2004 NFL season]] first in the AFC East with a 14–2 record. On January 16, 2005, Samuel earned a start in a playoff game for the first time in his career during a 20–3 victory against the [[2004 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in the AFC Divisional Round. On February 6, 2005, Samuel started in [[Super Bowl XXXIX]] and recorded four combined tackles (three solo) and led his team with four pass deflections as the Patriots defeated the [[2004 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] 24–21.

====2005====
The New England Patriots promoted [[Eric Mangini]] to defensive coordinator after [[Romeo Crennel]] accepted the head coach position with the [[Cleveland Browns]]. He entered training camp as a candidate to become the No. 1 starting cornerback following the departure of [[Ty Law]]. He competed for the role against [[Tyrone Poole]], [[Randall Gay]], [[Duane Starks]], and [[Chad Scott]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Corner looks familiar: Samuel, Gay back to man old roles| url=https://www.milforddailynews.com/story/sports/2005/09/14/corner-looks-familiar-samuel-gay/41163204007/ |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=milforddailynews.com | date=September 14, 2005|author=
Michael Felger}}</ref> He began the season as the No. 1 starting cornerback, alongside Tyrone Poole. In Week 1, Tyrone Poole injured his ankle and was replaced by Randall Gay as he remained inactive for the rest of the season.

In Week 8, he set a season-high with seven solo tackles, made two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Kelly Holcomb]] to wide receiver [[Eric Moulds]] as the Patriots defeated the [[2005 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] 21–16.<ref name="PFR5"/> The following week, Samuels set a season-high with eight combined tackles (six solo) and made two pass deflections during a 21–40 loss to the [[2005 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Injury Report| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2005-dec-29-sp-nflinjury29-story.html| access-date=May 26, 2025| website=[[Los Angeles Times]]| date=December 29, 2005}}</ref> He was inactive as the Patriots lost 26–28 against the [[2005 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] in Week 17. He finished with a title of 54 combined tackles (44 solo), 13 pass deflections, and three interceptions in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career"/>

The  [[2005 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] finished second in the AFC East with a 10–6 record to clinch a Wildcard berth. On January 7, 2006, Samuels made four solo tackles, three pass deflections, and returned an interception thrown by [[Byron Leftwich]] to wide receiver [[Reggie Williams (wide receiver)|Reggie Williams]] for a 73–yard touchdown during a 28–3 victory against the [[2005 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the AFC Wild-Card Game. On January 14, 2006, Samuels started in the AFC Divisional Round and recorded three solo tackles, made three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Jake Plummer]] to wide receiver [[Ashley Lelie]] as the Patriots lost 13–27 at the [[2005 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]].<ref name="PFR5">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2005)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

====2006====
The [[2006 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] promoted linebackers coach [[Dean Pees]] to defensive coordinator following the departure of [[Eric Mangini]], who became the head coach of the [[New York Jets]]. Samuel entered training camp slated as the ''de facto'' No. 1 starting cornerback following the departures of [[Tyrone Poole]] and [[Duane Starks]]. Head coach Bill Belichick named Samuel and [[Ellis Hobbs]] the starting cornerbacks to begin the season.

On October 8, 2006, Samuel made six solo tackles, two pass deflections, and had two interceptions on passes thrown by [[Joey Harrington]] as the Patriots defeated the [[2006 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] 20–10. This was his first career performance with multiple interceptions. He was sidelined for the Patriots' 35–0 victory at the [[2006 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in Week 11 due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pats Aren't Underestimating Favre|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/pats-aren-t-underestimating-favre-136581 |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Patriots.com| date=November 16, 2006}}</ref> In Week 12, he set a season-high with eight solo tackles, made three pass deflections, and set a career-high with three interceptions off passes thrown by [[Rex Grossman]] during a 17–13 victory against the [[2006 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]].<ref name="PFR6">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2006)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> His three interceptions tied the Patriots' single game interception record.<ref name="College"/> The following week, he recorded one solo tackle, set a season-high with four pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Jon Kitna]] to wide receiver [[Corey Bradford]] as the Patriots defeated the [[2006 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] 28–21.<ref>{{cite web| title=Detroit Lions at New England Patriots - December 16th, 2006| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612030nwe.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 31, 2006, Samuel made two solo tackles, tied his season-high of four pass deflections, and picked off two pass attempts by [[Vince Young]] during a 40–23 victory at the [[2006 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]]. He had one of the best seasons in his career in 2006, setting career-highs with 64 combined tackles (59 solo), 24 pass deflections, and 10 interceptions, while appearing in 15 games with 15 starts.<ref name="career"/> His 10 interceptions tied Broncos' cornerback [[Champ Bailey]] for the most interceptions in 2006. His 10 interceptions is the second most in the Patriots' franchise history for a single season, only behind [[Ron Hall (defensive back)|Ron Hall]], who had 11 interceptions [[1964 NFL season|(1964)]].

The [[2006 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] finished atop the AFC East with a 12–4 record during the [[2006 NFL season]], to clinch a playoff berth. On January 7, 2007, Samuel recorded three solo tackles, made three pass deflections, and had a pick-six after picking off a pass by [[Chad Pennington]] to wide receiver [[Justin McCareins]] and returned it 36–yards for a touchdown during a 37–16 win against the [[2006 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] in the AFC Wild-Card Game.
<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - New York Jets at New England Patriots - January 7th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200701070nwe.htm |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 21, 2007, Samuel started in the [[AFC Championship Game]] and made two solo tackles, three pass deflections, and returned an interception thrown by [[Peyton Manning]] to wide receiver [[Marvin Harrison]] and returned it 39–yards for a touchdown as the Patriots lost 34–38 at the [[2006 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFC Championship - New England Patriots at Indianapolis Colts - January 21st, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200701210clt.htm |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Colts eliminated the Patriots from the playoffs and advanced to the Super Bowl as they defeated the [[2006 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] 29–17 to win [[Super Bowl XLI]].

====2007====
On February 16, 2007, the [[2007 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] opted to assign the [[franchise tag]] on Samuel. On August 27, 2007, Samuel signed his franchise tag, for one–year, $7.79 million tender after he held out for the entire training camp and the majority of the preseason, as he was seeking a long-term contract offer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pats, cornerback Samuel agree on deal |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/patriots/2007-08-28-moves_N.htm |work=[[USA Today]] |date=August 28, 2007 }}</ref> It was reported by ''The Boston Globe'', that his agreement with the Patriots included a contract stipulation that stated the Patriots would not be able to place the franchise tag on Samuel for the second consecutive season if he played 60% of the snaps on defense at the conclusion of the [[2007 NFL season]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Christopher L. |last=Gasper |author2=Reiss, Mike |title=Did Eagles' plan vs. Patriots warm up the copy machine? |url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/football/patriots/articles/2007/11/27/warming_up_copy_machine/ |work=The Boston Globe |date=November 27, 2007 }}</ref> 

Due to his absence during training camp, the Patriots held a competition between [[Randall Gay]] and [[Chad Scott]] to name his replacement.<ref>{{cite web| title=Cause to be Gay at CB| url=https://www.telegram.com/story/news/local/north/2007/07/31/cause-to-be-gay-at/52834157007/ |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Telegram.com| date=July 27, 2007}}</ref> Head coach Bill Belichick named Randall Gay and [[Ellis Hobbs]] as the starting cornerbacks to begin the season. On September 8, 2007, the Patriots officially activated Samuel and added him to their active roster. He began the season as the primary backup cornerback.<ref>{{cite web| title=Patriots' Samuel activated for opener against the Jets| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3010937 |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=Len Pasquerelli| date=September 8, 2007}}</ref>

On October 1, 2007, Samuel set a season-high with four solo tackles, made two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Carson Palmer]] to wide receiver [[Chad Ochocinco]] during a 34–13 victory at the [[2007 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. The following week, he recorded two solo tackles, broke up two pass attempts, and intercepted a pass by [[Derek Anderson (American football)|Derek Anderson]] to wide receiver [[Joe Jurevicius]] as the Patriots defeated the [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] 34–17 in Week 5. This marked his third consecutive game with an interception. In Week 12, Samuel made three solo tackles, three pass deflections, set a season-high with two interceptions, and returned one for a touchdown during a 31–28 win against the [[2007 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]]. On the opening drive, Samuel had a pick-six, intercepting a pass by [[A. J. Feeley]] to running back [[Brian Westbrook]] and returned it 40–yards for a touchdown. He helped secure their victory by intercepting a pass by A. J. Feeley to wide receiver [[Kevin Curtis]] with 3:58 remaining in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web| title=Philadelphia Eagles at New England Patriots - November 26th, 2007| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200711250nwe.htm| access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> In Week 14, he set a season-high with five combined tackles (three solo) and had one pass deflection during a 34–13 win against the [[2007 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref name="PFR7">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2007)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 46 combined tackles (43 solo), 18 pass deflections, six interceptions, and one touchdown in 16 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career"/> He was voted to the [[Pro Bowl]] for the first time in his career.

The [[2007 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] were undefeated in [[2007 NFL season|2007]], finishing with a record of 16–0. On January 20, 2008, Samuel started in the [[AFC Championship Game]] and recorded three solo tackles, made two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Philip Rivers]] to wide receiver [[Chris Chambers]] during a 21–12 victory against the [[2007 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web| title=AFC Championship Game - San Diego Chargers at New England Patriots - January 20th, 2008| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801200nwe.htm| access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> On February 3, 2008, Samuel started in [[Super Bowl XLII]] and recorded two combined tackles (one solo) and made one pass deflection. Late in the fourth quarter, with 1:20 remaining and the Patriots leading 14–10, Samuel dropped a crucial interception on a pass attempt thrown by [[Eli Manning]] to wide receiver [[David Tyree]] that would have sealed the Patriots victory. On the following play, Manning completed a 32-yard pass to Tyree, which became famously known as the [[Helmet Catch]]. The [[2007 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] would have a last-minute comeback victory, defeating the New England Patriots 17–14 to win Super Bowl XLII and ended the Patriots 18 game undefeated streak.<ref name="n679">{{cite web | title=Inside the most improbable Super Bowl-winning drives ever: Six late-game marches that flipped the script | website=ESPN.com | url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/35466986/most-improbable-super-bowl-winning-drives-all-how-six-nfl-teams-flipped-fourth-quarter-win-probability-win-championship | access-date=2024-10-12}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:20090104 Asante Samuel (22).JPG|thumb|Samuel in the 2009 NFC Wild Card Game]]

====2008====
On February 29, 2008, within minutes of the official start of free agency, it was reported that Samuel would be meeting with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], as he was considered as one of the sought-after free agents.<ref>[http://community.foxsports.com/blogs/Alex_Marvez/2008/02/28/Source_Porter_Samuel_set_for_visits Source: Porter, Samuel set for visits • Everybody Loves a Smart Alex - FOX Sports Blogs<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080304055826/http://community.foxsports.com/blogs/Alex_Marvez/2008/02/28/Source_Porter_Samuel_set_for_visits |date=March 4, 2008 }}</ref> Later that day, the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] signed Samuel to a six–year, $59.47 million contract as an unrestricted free agent, that includes $6.60 million guaranteed and an initial [[signing bonus]] of $6.00 million.<ref name="spotrac"/> Upon being signed, Samuel was quoted as saying, “I just want to be able to win and get back to the Super Bowl.” He entered training camp slated as the ''de facto'' No. 1 starting cornerback under defensive coordinator [[Jim Johnson (American football)|Jim Johnson]]. Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named him a starting cornerback to begin the season and started him alongside [[Sheldon Brown (American football)|Sheldon Brown]] and nickelback [[Lito Sheppard]].

On September 15, 2007, Samuel made two solo tackles, one pass deflection, and had his first interception as a member of the Eagles during a 37–41 loss at the [[2008 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]]. His first interception of the season was on a pass attempt thrown by [[Tony Romo]] to wide receiver [[Miles Austin]]. The following week, he set a season-high with six combined tackles (four solo), made two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Ben Roethlisberger]] to wide receiver [[Nate Washington]] in Week 3. He was inactive as the Eagles defeated the [[2008 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] 48–20 in Week 13 due to an injury to his neck that was described as a stinger.<ref>{{cite web| title=Joselio Hanson replaces Asante Samuel at left cornerback for Eagles| url=https://www.nj.com/eagles/2008/11/joselio_hanson_not_lito_sheppa.html |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=NJ.com| date=November 27, 2008| author=John Nalbone}}</ref> On December 15, 2008, Samuel made one solo tackle, one pass deflection, and returned an interception thrown by [[Ken Dorsey]] to wide receiver [[Donte Stallworth]] for a 50–yard touchdown during a 30–10 victory against the [[2008 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref name="PFR8">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2008)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 36 combined tackles (32 solo), tied his career-high with 24 pass deflections, made four interceptions, and scored one touchdown in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career"/>

The [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] finished the [[2008 NFL season]] second in the [[NFC East]] with a
9–6–1 record, earning a Wildcard berth. On January 4, 2009, Samuel made one solo tackle, a pass deflection, and returned an interception on a pass by [[Tarvaris Jackson]] thrown to wide receiver [[Sidney Rice]] 44–yards for a touchdown during a 26–14 victory at the [[2008 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] in the NFC Wild-Card Game. He set an NFL record with his fourth interception returned for a touchdown in the postseason.<ref>{{cite news|title=Eagles CB Samuel sets NFL playoff record |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=503482 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090122042233/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=503482 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 22, 2009 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=January 4, 2009 }}</ref> The following week, Samuel recorded four solo tackles, made one pass deflection, and picked off a pass by [[Eli Manning]] thrown to wide receiver [[Domenik Hixon]] as the Eagles won the NFC Divisional Round 23–11 at the [[2008 New York Giants season|New York Giants]].<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.tcpalm.com/news/2009/jan/12/eli-mannings-anything-but-super-against-eagles/ |title=Eli Manning's anything but Super against Eagles |last=Jensen |first=Mike |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=January 12, 2009 }}</ref> On January 18, 2009, Samuel started in the [[NFC Championship Game]] and recorded three solo tackles as the Eagles lost 25–32 at the [[2008 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]].

====2009====
On May 18, 2009, the [[2009 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] promoted defensive backs coach [[Sean McDermott]] to defensive coordinator following the departure of Jim Johnson due to a medical leave. McDermott chose to retain Samuel and Sheldon Brown as the starting cornerbacks to begin the season.

On September 13, 2009, Samuel started in the Eagles' season-opener at the [[2009 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] and made three solo tackles, set a season-high with two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Jake Delhomme]] to wide receiver [[Steve Smith Sr.]] as they won 38–10. In Week 5, he made four solo tackles, two pass deflections, and set a season-high with two interceptions on passes thrown by [[Josh Johnson (quarterback)|Josh Johnson]] during a 33–14 win against the [[2009 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In Week 12, he had two pass deflections and tied his season-high of two interceptions on pass attempts by [[Jason Campbell]] during a 27–24 win against the [[2009 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]].
On December 20, 2009, Samuel made four solo tackles, a pass deflection, a fumble recovery, and had his eighth interception of the on a pass by [[Alex Smith]] to tight end [[Vernon Davis]] during a 27–13 win against the [[2009 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]]. The following week, he set a season-high with five solo tackles, made a pass deflection, and had his ninth interception of the season on a pass attempt by [[Kyle Orton]] to tight end [[Tony Scheffler]] as the Eagles defeated the [[2009 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] 30–27 in Week 16. He started all 16 games for the first time in his career and finished with a total of 40 combined tackles (39 solo), 16 pass deflections, nine interceptions, one forced fumble, and a fumble recovery.<ref name="career"/> With nine interceptions in 2009, Samuel tied for the most interceptions that season, along with [[Jairus Byrd]], [[Charles Woodson]], and [[Darren Sharper]]. His nine interceptions tied for second in franchise history for most interceptions in a single season, with [[Don Burroughs]] ([[1960 NFL season|1960]]) and [[Ed Bawel|Ed "Bibbles" Bawel]] ([[1955 NFL season|1955]]). He was selected to the [[2010 Pro Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/probowl.htm |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 54th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2011]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2011-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
====2010====
He returned to training camp as the No. 1 starting cornerback. Samuel and Ellis Hobbs began the season as the starting cornerbacks for the second consecutive season. In Week 4, Samuel recorded two solo tackles, before exiting in the fourth quarter of a 12–17 loss to the [[2010 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]] after he suffered a [[concussion]] while making a tackle on tight end [[Mike Sellers]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Redskins Add 4 Eagles to Endangered Species List|url=https://www.hogshaven.com/2010/10/4/1729884/redskins-add-4-eagles-to-endangered-species-list |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=hogshaven.com |date=October 4, 2010}}</ref> He subsequently remained inactive for the Eagles' 27–24 victory at the [[2010 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] in Week 5 due to his concussion. On October 17, 2010, he made four combined tackles (three solo), set a season-high with three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] to tight end [[Tony Gonzalez]] as the Eagles defeated the [[2010 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] 31–17.<ref>{{cite web| title=Atlanta Falcons at Philadelphia Eagles - October 17th, 2010| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010170phi.htm|access-date=May 28, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> In Week 7, he made three combined tackles (two solo), one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Kerry Collins]] to wide receiver [[Kenny Britt]] during a 19–37 loss at the [[2010 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]]. On November 7, 2010, he made two pass deflections and set a season-high with two interceptions during a 26–24 win against the [[2010 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. He sealed the Eagles' victory with 18 seconds remaining, by intercepting a pass attempt by [[Peyton Manning]] to wide receiver [[Blair White]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Indianapolis Colts at Philadelphia Eagles - November 7, 2010| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201011070phi.htm |date=May 28, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> In Week 11, Samuel recorded two solo tackles, made two pass deflections, and tied his season-high of two interceptions on pass attempts by [[Eli Manning]] during a 27–17 win against the [[2010 New York Giants season|New York Giants]].<ref name="PFR10">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2010)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> During the game, Samuel injured his knee while recovering a fumble and subsequently remained inactive for the next three games (Weeks 12–14). He was sidelined as the Eagles lost 13–14 to the [[2010 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] in Week 17 after reinjuring his knee.<ref>{{cite web| title=Vick inactive for Eagles-Cowboys game| url=https://www.columbian.com/news/2011/jan/02/vick-inactive-for-eagles-cowboys-game/| access-date=May 28, 2025| website=Columbian.com| date=January 2, 2011}}</ref> He finished the [[2010 NFL season]] with a total of 26 combined tackles (22 solo), 14 pass deflections, nine interceptions, and one forced fumble in 11 games and 10 starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2011====
On February 2, 2011, the [[2011 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] unexpectedly promoted offensive lineman coach [[Juan Castillo (American football)|Juan Castillo]] to defensive coordinator after [[Sean McDermott]] was fired following the [[2010 NFL season]]. Castillo retained Samuel as the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin training camp. On July 28, 2011, the Eagles acquired [[Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie]] in a trade with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and also signed top unrestricted free agent [[Nnamdi Asomugha]] the following day. Head coach Andy Reid named Samuel and Nnamdi Asomugha the starting cornerbacks to begin the season along with nickelback Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie.<ref>{{cite web| title=Eagles Release First Depth Chart| url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-release-first-depth-chart-5407431 |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=philadelphiaeagles.com| date=August 8, 2011}}</ref>

On September 11, 2011, Samuel started in the Eagles' season-opener at the [[2011 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]] and set a season-high with five solo tackles as they won 31–13.<ref name="PFR11">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2011)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> The following week, he recorded two solo tackles, set a season-high with two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] to wide receiver [[Julio Jones]] during a 31–35 loss at the [[2011 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] in Week 2. On October 28, 2011, following practice, Samuel openly criticized the Eagles' front office during an interview and expressed his frustration about repeated trade rumors that immediately began after the Eagles acquired Nnamdi Asomugha and Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie during training camp.<ref name="office">{{cite web| title=Asante Samuel: Eagles' front office "playing fantasy football"| url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/asante-samuel-eagles-front-office-playing-fantasy-football |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=NBCSports.com| date=October 28, 2011}}</ref>
{{quote box
|align=right
|width=50%
|quote="Couple people upstairs might not want me, but who cares. They've probably never played football. It's a business and they run it like a business and they're going to do what they need to do. They're playing with a lot of money, playing fantasy football, doing their thing."
(When asked if he was referring to [[General manager (American football)|GM]] [[Howie Roseman]] and President [[Joe Banner]])
"Howie and Joe? I don't know, do they fit the comment I made? There ya go. You think they're upstairs playing fantasy football with the owner's money? That sucks, doesn’t it?. Each trade deadline for your name to be flying around and you’re supposed to be the leader of this team."
|source=–Asante Samuel 
}}
On November 20, 2011, Samuel made four combined tackles (three solo), two pass deflections, and had a pick-six after intercepting a pass attempt by [[John Skelton (American football)|John Skelton]] to wide receiver [[Larry Fitzgerald]] and returning it for a 20–yard touchdown as the Eagles lost 17–21 against the [[2011 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. In Week 15, he made two combined tackles (one solo), one pass deflection, and had his last interception as a member of the Eagles on a pass by [[Mark Sanchez]] to wide receiver [[Santonio Holmes]] as the Eagles defeated the [[2011 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] 45–19.<ref>{{cite web| title=New York Jets at Philadelphia Eagles - December 17th, 2011|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112180phi.htm |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> Due to a hamstring injury, Samuel was inactive for the last two games of the season (Weeks 16–17). He finished his last season with the Philadelphia Eagles with a total of 34 combined tackles (30 solo), 10 pass deflections, three interceptions, one touchdown, a forced fumble, and one fumble recovery in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career"/>

===Atlanta Falcons===
====2012====
On April 25, 2012, the [[Atlanta Falcons]] acquired Samuel in a trade with the [[2012 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] and in return received a [[Bryce Brown|seventh-round pick]] (229th overall) in [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-04-25 |title=Falcons trade for Samuel, who redoes deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7853300/atlanta-falcons-acquire-asante-samuel-philadelphia-eagles |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> The Falcons only agreed to the trade after Samuel agreed to restructure his contract that still has two–years, $21.30 million remaining.<ref>{{cite web| title=Asante Samuel dealt to Falcons| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7853300/atlanta-falcons-acquire-asante-samuel-philadelphia-eagles |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=ESPN.com| date=April 25, 2012}}</ref> The [[2012 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] signed Samuel to a three–year, $14.70 million contract extension that included $2.25 million guaranteed.<ref name="spotrac"/>
[[File:Asante Samuel 2013.jpg|thumb|200px|Samuel at Falcons training camp in 2013]]
The Falcons entered trade talks with the Eagles to possibly acquire Samuel after Brent Grimes publicly refused to sign his franchise tag and would hold out until he received a long-term deal.<ref>{{cite web| title=Grimes Among the League's Best at Corner Position| url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/grimes-among-the-league-s-best-at-corner-position-7831833 |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=AtlantaFalcons.com| date=June 26, 2012}}</ref> Throughout training camp, he competed to earn a role as a starting cornerback against [[Dunta Robinson]] and [[Brent Grimes]] under defensive coordinator [[Mike Nolan]]. Head coach [[Mike Smith (American football coach)|Mike Smith]] named Samuel a backup and listed him as the No. 3 cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starters Brent Grimes and Dunta Robinson.

In Week 2, he set a season-high with seven combined tackles (six solo) during a 27–21 victory against the [[2012 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]]. He entered the game as a replacement for Brent Grimes who exited due to an injury.<ref name="PFR12">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2012)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> On September 11, 2012, the Falcons officially placed Brent Grimes on injured reserve due to a torn Achilles tendon. Samuel was therefore promoted to the No. 2 starting cornerback for the rest of the season. On October 14, 2012, Samuel made four solo tackles, one pass deflection, and led the Falcons to a 23–20 comeback victory against the [[2012 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] with a pick-six late in the fourth quarter. Samuel intercepted a pass attempt thrown by [[Carson Palmer]] to wide receiver [[Denarius Moore]] and returned it 79–yards for a touchdown with 3:54 remaining. In Week 10, he recorded two solo tackles, set a season-high with three pass deflections, and picked off a pass attempt by [[Drew Brees]] to wide receiver [[Marques Colston]] during a 27–31 loss at the [[2012 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. On November 29, 2012, Samuel exited early in the first quarter of a 23–13 win against the Saints after re-injuring his shoulder that he originally injured while tackling [[Larry Fitzgerald]] in Week 11 against the [[2012 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. In Week 15, Samuel recorded one tackle, made two pass deflections, and intercepted the first pass attempt by Eli Manning that was thrown to wide receiver [[Hakeem Nicks]] as the Falcons routed the [[2012 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] 34–0. On December 30, 2012, Samuel made two solo tackles, two pass deflections, and had his third consecutive game with an interception after picking off a pass by [[Josh Freeman]] to wide receiver [[Tiquan Underwood]] during a 17–22 loss against the [[2012 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He finished the [[2012 NFL season]] with 37 combined tackles (34 solo), 15 pass deflections, five interceptions, and a single touchdown in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career"/>
====2013====
Following the departures of [[Dunta Robinson]] and [[Brent Grimes]], the [[2013 Atlanta Falcons season|Falcons]] selected [[Desmond Trufant]] in the first-round (22nd overall) and [[Robert Alford (American football)|Robert Alford]] in the second-round (60th overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. Throughout training camp, Samuel competed against Desmond Trufant, [[Robert McClain]], and Robert Alford to earn a starting role at cornerback. Head coach Mike Smith named Samuel the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin the season, alongside Desmond Trufant.<ref>{{cite web| title=A look at the Falcons current depth chart| url=https://www.thefalcoholic.com/2013/8/4/4587532/atlanta-falcons-depth-chart-preseason |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=thefalcoholic.com| date=August 4, 2013| author=Alex Welch}}</ref> 

Samuel was inactive in Week 1, as the Falcons lost 17–23 at the [[2013 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]] due to an injury to his thigh.<ref>{{cite web| title=Falcons vs. Saints inactives, Week 1: Asante Samuel out for Atlanta| url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/9/8/4707320/saints-falcons-2013-inactive-list-nfl-week-1 |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=SBNation.com| date=September 8, 2013}}</ref> He was inactive again as the Falcons lost 23–30 against the [[2013 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in Week 4, due to his lingering thigh injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=Asante Samuel Injury: Cornerback Inactive Against Patriots| url=https://www.thefalcoholic.com/2013/9/29/4784744/asante-samuel-injury-cornerback-inactive-against-patriots |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=thefalcoholic.com| date=September 29, 2013| author=Dave Choate}}</ref> On October 27, 2013, Samuel recorded three solo tackles, broke up a pass, and had his last career interception after picking off a pass by [[Carson Palmer]] to wide receiver [[Andre Roberts (American football)|Andre Roberts]] during a 13–27 loss at the [[2013 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. The following week, he set a season-high with eight solo tackles and made one pass deflection during a 10–34 loss at the [[2013 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] in Week 9.<ref name="PFR13">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Asante Samuel Game Logs (2013)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20.htm |access-date=May 27, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>  Entering Week 14, head coach Mike Smith chose to bench Samuel and listed him inactive as a healthy scratch, replacing him with Robert Alford at the [[2013 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]]. He was benched again and was listed as inactive as a healthy scratch for the last two games of the season in lieu of Robert Alford.<ref>{{cite web| title=Will Asante Samuel Be Cut In The Off-season| url=https://www.thefalcoholic.com/2013/12/11/5193106/will-the-falcons-purge-veterans-again-in-the-off-season |access-date=May 28, 2025| website=thefalcoholic.com| date=December 11, 2013| author=Dave Choate}}</ref> Although Samuel began the season as the Falcons' No. 1 starting cornerback, by season's end he was listed as the No. 5 cornerback on the depth chart, behind Desmond Trufant, Robert Alford, Robert McClain, and [[Dominique Franks]]. He finished the season with 30 combined tackles (29 solo), four pass deflections, and one interception in 11 games and 10 starts.<ref name="career"/>

On February 5, 2014, the Falcons released him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs20/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Florio, Mike |title=Falcons dump Asante Samuel, Stephen Nicholas |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/05/falcons-dump-asante-samuel-stephen-nicholas/ |work=[[Profootballtalk.com]] |date=February 5, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2014}}</ref>

'''Atiyyah Ramadan Ellison''' [ah-TEE-ah] (born September 29, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]].

Ellison was also a member of the [[Houston Texans]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], and [[New England Patriots]].

He now works at the [[University of Missouri]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]] as the Director of Player Development - Football.

==Early life==
As a senior at [[Parkway South High School]] in [[St. Louis, Missouri]], Ellison had three [[quarterback sack|sacks]] and 47 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]]. He was ranked one of the top defensive lineman in the Midwest, won All-State honors, and was an All-Metro choice. Ellison also was a standout [[basketball]] player and received all-conference honors his senior year. He owns his high school [[shot put]] record and competed at the state track meet his junior and senior years.

Parkway South High School retired Ellison's jersey in 2006.

==College career==

===Coffeyville Community College===
Ellison attended [[Coffeyville Community College]] in [[Coffeyville, Kansas]], for two seasons, where he [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed in 2000. As a freshman in 2001, Ellison started 9 of 10 games, recording 57 tackles and five sacks. Inducted into the Coffeyville Hall of Fame in 2016.

===University of Missouri===
After community college, Ellison attended the [[University of Missouri]], where as a sophomore in 2002 he played in 12 games (9 starts), finishing with 39 tackles and two forced fumbles at [[defensive end]]. In 2003, Ellison earned third-team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] honors after recording 72 tackles, four sacks, and two forced fumbles. As a senior in 2004, Ellison played in 11 games, finishing with 60 tackles and 2.5 sacks, earning first-team All-Big 12 honors.

==Professional career==

===Carolina Panthers===
Ellison was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round (89th overall) of the [[2005 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was waived by Carolina during final cuts on September 3, 2005, and re-signed to their [[practice squad]] two days later. On September 14, 2005, he was promoted to the 53-man roster, but was waived again on September 24, 2005. He returned to the practice squad on September 27, 2005, and was elevated to the active roster again on October 31, 2005, where he spent the remainder of the season as an inactive. He was waived by the Panthers on September 2, 2006.

===Houston Texans===
The [[Houston Texans]] claimed Ellison off waivers on September 3, 2006, but waived him on September 7, 2006, before the start of the regular season.

===Baltimore Ravens===
Ellison was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on September 12, 2006, and was elevated to the 53-man roster on December 4, 2006. He was inactive for three games before being placed on [[injured reserve]] with a shoulder injury on December 30, 2006. He was waived by the Ravens on September 1, 2007, and re-signed to their practice squad the next day.

===San Francisco 49ers===
The [[San Francisco 49ers]] signed Ellison to their 53-man roster off the Ravens' practice squad on September 5, 2007. He was inactive for the entire 2007 season and was waived by the 49ers on August 30, 2008, and re-signed to the 49ers' practice squad the next day.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Ellison off the 49ers' practice squad on December 10, 2008, but he was inactive for the final three games of the regular season. Ellison made his NFL debut as a reserve in Week 1 of the [[2009 Jacksonville Jaguars season|2009]] season. He went on to play in 15 games for the Jaguars in 2009, starting nine at defensive tackle. He finished the season with 28 tackles and one and a half sack. He was waived by the Jaguars on September 4, 2010.

===Kansas City Chiefs===
The [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed Ellison on October 20, 2010. He was inactive for one game before being waived on October 27, 2010.

===New England Patriots===
Ellison was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] on January 4, 2011, prior to their first [[2010–11 NFL playoffs|playoff]] game. He was waived on January 8, 2011.

'''Artose Deonce Pinner''' (born January 5, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the fourth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky Wildcats]].

==Early life==
Pinner attended [[Hopkinsville High School]] in Hopkinsville, Kentucky, and was a standout in football and [[Track and field|track]]. In track, he was a two-time Regional Champion in the 400 meter dash.

==College career==
He was a star running back for the [[University of Kentucky]] between 1999 and 2002, running for 1414 yards in 2002, second-most in a single season in school history to [[Moe Williams]].

==Professional career==
Pinner was selected with the second pick of the fourth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]] by the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He increased his rushing total in each of his first three seasons in the league, going from 99 yards in 2003 to 174 yards in 2004 to 349 yards in 2005. Through the 2005 season, Pinner scored five touchdowns, all rushing.

Pinner was cut by the Detroit Lions in 2006 and was quickly claimed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]].  He had his best game statistically, which was his first start in the NFL, on December 10, 2006, when he ran for 125 yards and three touchdowns against his former [[Detroit Lions]]. On May 1, 2008, he returned to the [[Detroit Lions]]. After the 2008 preseason, he was waived by the Lions during final cuts on August 30, 2008.

==Post-retirement==
Pinner returned to the University of Kentucky in the summer of 2013 to complete his degree in [[media studies]]. He graduated in December 2013.<ref name=returnToUK>{{cite web|last=Ramsey|first=Guy|title=Former star running back Pinner keeps word, returns to UK to graduate|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/12/former-star-running-back-pinner-keeps-word-returns-to-uk-to-graduate.html|work=26 December 2013|publisher=[[University of Kentucky]]|access-date=27 December 2013|archive-date=December 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131228112635/http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/12/former-star-running-back-pinner-keeps-word-returns-to-uk-to-graduate.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Artis Hicks Jr.''' (born November 28, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis Tigers]] and was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2002.

Hicks also played for the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Washington Redskins]], and [[Cleveland Browns]].

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Hicks signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in April 2002 as an [[undrafted free agent]]. He made the active roster for the entire [[2002 NFL season|2002 season]]. In [[2003 NFL season|2003]], Hicks got his first start against the [[New York Giants]].

In April 2004, Hicks signed a multi-year contract extension with the Eagles.  He started at left guard for the [[2004 NFL season|2004 season]], including [[Super Bowl XXXIX]] in 2005 against the [[New England Patriots]].

===Minnesota Vikings===
In April 2006, the Eagles traded Hicks to the [[Minnesota Vikings]], where he started at right guard for the Vikings during the [[2006 NFL season|2006 season]].

===Washington Redskins===
On March 6, 2010, Hicks was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] as a free agent. On September 3, 2011, Washington released Hicks to waivers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Fitzgerald|first=Gary|title=Redskins' Roster Is At 53 After Final Cuts|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Roster-Is-At-53-After-Final-Cuts/e68e2fb9-0775-43db-be72-1d48b0a0c819|publisher=redskins.com|accessdate=September 3, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120802090355/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Roster-Is-At-53-After-Final-Cuts/e68e2fb9-0775-43db-be72-1d48b0a0c819|archive-date=August 2, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Hicks signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] on September 4, 2011.

===Miami Dolphins===
Hicks signed with the Miami Dolphins on March 15, 2012.<ref>[http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/03/15/dolphins-sign-artis-hicks-to-one-year-deal/ Dolphins sign Artis Hicks to one-year deal]</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to a neck injury on September 4.<ref>[http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/09/04/dolphins-lose-artis-hicks-for-season/ Dolphins lose Artis Hicks for season]</ref>

'''Artrell Hawkins Jr.''' (born November 24, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]] and was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the second round of the [[1998 NFL draft]].

Hawkins played cornerback for the Bengals, [[Carolina Panthers]] and later transitioned to safety for the [[New England Patriots]]. He finished his 10-year career as a member of the [[New York Jets]] prior to the 2008 season.

==Early life==
Artrell Hawkins Jr. was born the son of Artrell Hawkins Sr. and Aletha (Haselrig-Jones) Hawkins on November 24, 1976. He attended [[Bishop McCort High School]] in [[Johnstown, Pennsylvania]], where he was named conference offensive player of the year as a senior after rushing for a school record 26 touchdowns and 1,487 yards, including a single-game record 265 yards. He also lettered in basketball and baseball at Bishop McCort.

Hawkins' father, Artrell Hawkins Sr. was a three-year letterman at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] and was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] as a rookie free agent in 1980.

Hawkins attended the [[University of Cincinnati]], where he majored in business and lettered in football for four years (1994–1997) as a defensive back and kick returner under head coach [[Rick Minter]]. His senior year, the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Bearcats]] went 8–4 and played in the [[Humanitarian Bowl]], breaking the school's 47-year drought of not appearing in a bowl game. The Bearcats defeated [[Utah State Aggies football|Utah State University]], 35–19.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cstv.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/cinn/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/05FBmg-Records119-158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081002152101/http://www.cstv.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/cinn/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/05FBmg-Records119-158|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 2, 2008|title = CBS Sports - News, Live Scores, Schedules, Fantasy Games, Video and more}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Hawkins was selected by the Cincinnati Bengals in the second round of the [[1998 NFL draft]], where he played [[cornerback]] for six years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In his rookie year of 1998, he started in all 16 Bengals' games, recording 65 tackles, five assists, one sack and three interceptions.

In 1999, Hawkins played in 14 games (starting 13) and totaled 61 tackles and seven assists. In 2000, he played in all 16 games, starting six, and recorded 43 tackles and four assists.<ref name="pro-football-reference.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HawkAr20.htm|title = Artrell Hawkins Stats| website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] }}</ref>

In 2001, Hawkins rebounded and played in 14 games (starting 13), totaling 49 tackles, 10 assists, and three interceptions. In 2002, he started and played in 15 games, recording 69 tackles, seven assists, two sacks, and two interceptions, including a league-leading and team record 102-yard interception return for a touchdown on a pass by [[David Carr (American football)|David Carr]] in a 38–3 Bengals' win over the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.profootballhof.com/hof/release.aspx?release_id=2959|title=Reed rumbles 108 yards for NFL record {{!}} Longest interception returns by team|work=[[Pro Football Hall of Fame]]|date=November 24, 2008|accessdate=June 2, 2014}}</ref> In 2003, his sixth and final season with the Bengals, he played in 14 games, starting nine, with 50 tackles, five assists, and one interception.

After that season he signed for 2004 with the [[Carolina Panthers]], for whom he played 14 games (starting four) with 24 tackles, five assists and one interception.

For the 2005 season, Hawkins joined the [[New England Patriots]], playing in five games (starting four) with 11 tackles, six assists and one sack. In 2006, he played in 14 games for the Patriots, starting 12 games and recording 54 tackles, 19 assists, and one interception.<ref name="pro-football-reference.com"/> He was released by the Patriots during the summer of 2007.<ref name="thejetsblog.com">{{cite web|url=http://thejetsblog.com/news/news-jets-sign-s-artrell-hawkins/ |title=News: Jets Sign S Artrell Hawkins | the Jets Blog |accessdate=2013-09-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928164831/http://thejetsblog.com/news/news-jets-sign-s-artrell-hawkins/ |archivedate=2013-09-28 }}</ref>

After sitting out the 2007 season, Hawkins signed with the [[New York Jets]] in February, 2008.<ref name="thejetsblog.com"/> He announced his retirement on August 1, 2008, prior to the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jetnation.com/2008/08/01/artrell-hawkins-retires/|title=Artrell Hawkins Retires|date=August 2008}}</ref>

His younger brother, [[Andrew Hawkins]], retired from playing in the league in July 2017, after stints with the Bengals and Browns.

Since retiring, Hawkins has been a fixture on Cincinnati sportstalk radio, beginning as a University of Cincinnati sideline reporter and also various co-hosting and guest duties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cincinnati.com/blogs/tv/2012/01/27/artrell-hawkins-nearly-quit-radio/ |title=Artrell Hawkins nearly quit radio | TV and Media Blog |accessdate=2013-09-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927045532/http://cincinnati.com/blogs/tv/2012/01/27/artrell-hawkins-nearly-quit-radio/ |archivedate=2013-09-27 }}</ref> Hawkins also is a weekly contributor to the Bengals Radio Network.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.artrellhawkins.com/services |title=Services | Artrell Hawkins |access-date=2011-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426011924/http://www.artrellhawkins.com/services/ |archive-date=2012-04-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsportsradio.com/pages/allstations.html |title=Fox Sports Radio - All Stations |accessdate=2013-09-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130508141916/http://www.foxsportsradio.com/pages/allstations.html |archivedate=2013-05-08 }}</ref>

'''Aubrayo Razyo Franklin''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|b|r|eɪ|.|oʊ}}; born August 27, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]] and was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fifth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]].

He also played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[Indianapolis Colts]].

==Early life==
Franklin attended [[Science Hill High School]] in [[Johnson City, Tennessee]], and was a letterman in football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birchfield |first=Jeff |date=February 23, 2023 |title=Fulmer, Tri-Cities area have greatly impacted each other |url=https://www.johnsoncitypress.com/sports/college/fulmer-tri-cities-area-have-greatly-impacted-each-other/article_7b2da27a-b239-11ed-be48-2f55b11a4eea.html |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=Johnson City Press |language=en}}</ref> In football, as a senior, he was an All-Conference and an All-State honoree and finished his senior season with 12 sacks and 180 tackles.

==College career==
Franklin played [[college football]] at the [[University of Tennessee]] where he recorded 70 tackles and two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2010 |title=Witten Camp Inspires Former Science Hill Star Aubrayo Franklin |url=https://tricitiessports.com/witten-camp-inspires-former-science-hill-star-aubrayo-franklin-p43973-454.htm |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=TriCitiesSports.com |language=en}}</ref> He majored in arts and sciences.

===Baltimore Ravens===
Franklin was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fifth round (146th overall) in the [[2003 NFL draft]], after being projected as a late sixth round pick.<ref>{{cite news |title=2003 NFL Draft - Aubrayo Franklin |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2003/draft/players/14113.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030621084401/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2003/draft/players/14113.html |archive-date=June 21, 2003 |work=SI.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=March 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his rookie year, he only appeared in one game recording one tackle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2003 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2003/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

He played in ten games, starting nine, for the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] during the [[2004 NFL Europe season]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-frankaub001 | title=Aubrayo Franklin | publisher=statscrew.com | accessdate=June 2, 2024}}</ref> In his second season with the Ravens in 2004, he contributed to the team by making six appearances and two tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2004 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2004/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2005, Franklin played in 15 games and notched up 20 tackles and his first career sack at the [[Denver Broncos]] on December 11.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2005 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2005/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He also made his first career start a week later against the [[Green Bay Packers]]. In his final season with the Ravens, he played in 14 games recording 17 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2006/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On March 3, 2007, Franklin signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]], reuniting himself with Coach [[Mike Nolan]], who was his defensive coordinator in Baltimore. In his first season with the team, he played in 14 games recording a career high 28 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2008 season, he appeared in 16 games and started 15. He finished with one sack, 46 total tackles, two passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2009 season, he started in all 16 games. He finished with two sacks, 36 total tackles, one interception, and three passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2010 season, he finished with 39 total tackles (38 solo), one pass defended, and one fumble recovery in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
Franklin signed a one-year contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on August 2, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Triplett |first=Mike |date=August 4, 2011 |title=New Orleans Saints revel in landing run stuffer Aubrayo Franklin |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/new-orleans-saints-revel-in-landing-run-stuffer-aubrayo-franklin/article_eaaff40c-3a5d-55c5-a959-1992ce92dbd3.html |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref>  In the 2011 season, he had 18 total tackles (12 solo) in 16 games and nine starts. The Saints elected to allow Franklin to test free agency following the 2011 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
On July 20, 2012, Franklin signed a one-year contract with the [[San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2012 |title=Aubrayo Franklin, San Diego Chargers agree to terms |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aubrayo-franklin-san-diego-chargers-agree-to-terms-09000d5d82ab2341 |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He appeared in 12 games and made nine starts. He finished with 20 total tackles (16 solo).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On March 19, 2013, Franklin signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Phillip B. |date=July 17, 2013 |title=Colts signing nose tackle Aubrayo Franklin raises questions about other players |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/philb/1/01/01/colts-signing-nose-tackle-aubrayo-franklin-raises-questions-about-other-players/2536347/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Josh |date=March 19, 2013 |title=Colts Sign Veteran DT Aubrayo Franklin |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2013/3/19/4124918/colts-sign-dt-aubrayo-franklin |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=Stampede Blue |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2013 season with 29 total tackles (17 solo) and one pass defended in 16 games and 15 starts. He started both of the Colts' postseason games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aubrayo Franklin 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAu20/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

On January 28, 2015, Franklin rejoined the 49ers to an entry-level coaching position under head coach [[Jim Tomsula]], who was his defensive line coach from 2007 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 10, 2015 |title=Aubrayo Franklin Returns to 49ers as Assistant Coach |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/aubrayo-franklin-returns-to-49ers-as-assistant-coach-14898441 |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=49ers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> After just 1 season, Tomsula was fired thus resulting in a large coaching overhaul that relieved Franklin of his duties.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2016 |title=49er quietly clean house in coaching staff |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/49er-quietly-clean-house-in-coaching-staff |access-date=March 16, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |publisher=Pro Football Talk |language=en-US}}</ref>

He forwent his senior season and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the third round (70 overall) of the [[2006 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |date=9 January 2006 |title=Ohio State CB Ashton Youboty to turn pro|agency=Associated Press |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/draft06/news/story?id=2285498 |access-date=16 January 2019 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} After five seasons with the Bills (2006–2010), he played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in 2011. ==Early life== Youboty was born in [[Monrovia, Liberia]], the oldest of four children for Jeannet Waylee.
