Youboty and his family eventually relocated to [[Houston, Texas]]. He attended [[Klein High School]], where he returned to graduate with the class of 2003 after participating as an early winter enrollee at the [[Ohio State University]]. As a freshman, he played football, basketball, and ran track. By the end of his freshman football season, he was moved up to the varsity football team, where he played [[cornerback]], [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]], [[wide receiver]], and returned kicks. As a three-year starter, he competed against many of Houston's most talented football players including Woodlands High School's [[Danny Amendola]]. His first college-football scholarship offer came from [[Nick Saban]] during the latter's tenure at [[Louisiana State University]] but Youboty eventually signed to play for [[Jim Tressel]] at the Ohio State University. ==College career== He passed up his senior year of eligibility at [[Ohio State University]] to enter the [[2006 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |date=9 January 2006 |title=Ohio State CB Ashton Youboty to pass up senior year |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft06/news/story?id=2285498 |access-date=30 April 2010 |website=ESPN.com |publisher=Associated Press}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 5 | height in = 11 3/4 | weight = 189 | dash = 4.44 | shuttle = 4.18 | cone drill = 6.96 | vertical = 36.0 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 0 | bench = 11 | arm span = 30 7/8 | hand span = 8 3/4 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/ashton-youboty/3200594f-5500-7285-6585-71283e97edbf |title=Ashton Youboty Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=December 22, 2024}}{{Cite web |title=2006 NFL Draft Scout Ashton Youboty College Football Profile |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=12439&DraftYear=2006 |access-date=January 28, 2024 |website=DraftScout.com}} }} ===Buffalo Bills=== Youboty was drafted in the third round (70th overall) of the [[2006 NFL draft]] by the [[Buffalo Bills]], joining [[Donte Whitner]] as the second [[Ohio State Buckeyes football]] player selected by the Bills in the draft.{{Cite web |title=2006 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2006/draft.htm |access-date=9 May 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=2006 Buffalo Bills Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/buf/2006_draft.htm |access-date=30 June 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He played with the Bills for the first five seasons of his career from 2006 to 2010. Youboty's best season in the NFL was 2007 when he appeared in eleven games for the Bills and was credited with 23 tackles (22 solo), a sack and an interception.{{Cite web |title=Ashton Youboty 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Y/YoubAs20/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=30 June 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} === Tampa Bay Buccaneers === Youboty signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on 15 August 2011. He was released on 29 August 2011.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Y/YoubAs20.htm | title=Ashton Youboty | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=May 16, 2024}} ===Jacksonville Jaguars=== The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Youboty on 15 November 2011.{{cite web | title=Jaguars sign CB Ashton Youboty, DE George Selvie | website=Jaguars.com | date=2011-11-15 | url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-cb-ashton-youboty-de-george-selvie-6293486 | access-date=2025-01-01}} In his first game, he recovered a fumble and returned it for a touchdown against the [[2011 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]] on 27 November 2011. Youboty was placed on [[Injured Reserve]] on 26 December 2011 after injuring his left hamstring. Youboty was released on 25 August 2012.{{Cite web |date=2012-08-25 |title=Veteran CB Youboty among 8 let go by Jaguars |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/trainingcamp12/story/_/id/8302930/veteran-cb-ashton-youboty-eight-players-let-go-jacksonville-jaguars |access-date=2024-12-21 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} ==Coaching career== Following the conclusion of his athletic career, Youboty worked as a [[Quality control coach]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football]] program.{{Cite web|url=http://uwbadgers.com/coaches.aspx?rc=814&path=football|title=Ashton Youboty {{!}} Football Coach|website=Wisconsin Athletics|language=en|access-date=16 January 2019}} After two seasons, he was elevated to senior defensive analyst. For the 2020 and 2021 seasons, Youboty served as the cornerbacks coach for the [[Youngstown State Penguins football]] team. In February 2022, Youboty joined [[Jeff Brohm]]'s staff at [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue]] as the cornerbacks coach.{{Cite web |last=Samuels |first=Doug |date=5 February 2022 |title=The Scoop - Saturday February 5, 2022 |url=https://footballscoop.com/thescoop/the-scoop-saturday-february-5-2022 |access-date=5 February 2022 |website=Football Scoop}} ==Personal life== The oldest of four children, he has one sister and two brothers. '''Atari David Bigby''' (born September 19, 1981) is a former [[American football]] [[Safety (American football position)|safety]]. He was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2005 after playing [[college football]] at the University of Central Florida (UCF).

Bigby was also a member of the [[New York Jets]], [[Green Bay Packers]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], and the [[San Diego Chargers]]. He won [[Super Bowl XLV]] defeating the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

==Early life==
Bigby attended [[Miami High School (Miami, Florida)|Miami High School]] in [[Miami, Florida]], where he [[Varsity letter|lettered]] three years in [[High school football|football]] and two in [[Track and field|track]], and also competed as a standout soccer player. He attended high school alongside several future professional athletes, including [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] [[Marquand Manuel]], [[Houston Texans]] [[wide receiver]] [[Andre Johnson]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] wide receiver [[Roscoe Parrish]], [[Philadelphia Eagles]] [[offensive lineman]] [[Jamaal Jackson]], and [[Miami Heat]] [[forward (basketball)|forward]] [[Udonis Haslem]]. 

As a prep player, Bigby played every position on the field except lineman. During his senior year, he recorded 72 tackles, four forced fumbles, and one interception on defense, while adding 500 receiving yards, 315 rushing yards, and nine touchdowns on offense. He earned second-team Class 6A all-state honors and also played in the Dade-Broward All-Star Game.<ref name="Bigby">{{Cite web |title=Atari Bigby's Bio at packers |url=http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070413003346/http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/ |archive-date=April 13, 2007 |access-date=September 11, 2007 |publisher=packers.com}}</ref>

==College career==
As a redshirt freshman at the University of Central Florida, Bigby played in 11 games and recorded 38 tackles.<ref name="Atari Bigby">{{Cite web |title=Atari Bigby |url=http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/#s7 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091203041026/http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/ |archive-date=December 3, 2009 |access-date=October 28, 2009}}</ref> During his time at UCF, he earned All-Conference honors twice in the Mid-American Conference (MAC).

==Professional career==

===Miami Dolphins===
After going undrafted in the [[2005 NFL draft]], Bigby was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 16, 2005. He was later waived by the Dolphins on July 25, 2005, prior to the start of the preseason.<ref name="Packers.com">{{Cite web |title=Packers.com > Team > Players > Atari Bigby |url=http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060116235722/http://www.packers.com/team/players/bigby_atari/ |archive-date=January 16, 2006 |access-date=April 18, 2010 |publisher=Packers.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Bigby was signed by the [[New York Jets]] on August 11, 2005. He was waived during final roster cuts on September 3, despite a standout performance in training camp.

===Green Bay Packers===
[[File:Atari Bigby celebrates his interception.jpg|right|thumb|Bigby celebrating an interception in 2009]]
Bigby was originally signed to the Packers' practice squad on November 1, 2005. He was promoted to the active roster on December 22, 2005, and made his NFL debut on December 25 against the [[Chicago Bears]].

Bigby was waived by the Packers at the end of the 2006 preseason,re-signed to the practice squad two days later. After spending the first ten weeks of the season on the Packers' practice squad, he was signed to the active roster on November 15, 2006. He recorded two tackles during the season. Bigby also played in NFL Europe for the Amsterdam Admirals, representing the Green Bay Packers.

After a very successful 2007 training camp and preseason, Bigby replaced starting strong safety [[Marquand Manuel]], who was released prior to the 2007 regular season. Bigby was named the NFC Defensive Player of the month for December 2007.<ref name="defpow">{{Cite web |title=Atari Bigby Voted Defensive Player Of The Week |url=http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2007/12/20/2/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080223062734/http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2007/12/20/2/ |archive-date=February 23, 2008 |access-date=December 23, 2007 |publisher=Packers.com}}</ref> He tied for the NFL lead with four interceptions during the month in just four games. The Packers posted a 3–1 record in December and clinched the [[NFC North]] division, securing the No. 2 seed in the NFC playoffs. Bigby recorded an interception in three of Green Bay's four December games, including a 22-yard interception in Week 14 and a career-high two interceptions the following week against St. Louis. He added another interception in the Packers' win over Detroit.

On January 12, Bigby started his first playoff game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He finished the game with seven tackles (one for a loss), a forced fumble, and a pass defensed. He delivered two notable hits, including one that caused a fumble by [[Marcus Pollard]] that was recovered by defensive end [[Aaron Kampman]], leading to a Packers scoring drive.

An [[exclusive-rights free agent]] in the 2008 offseason, Bigby signed a one-year tender deal with the Packers.<ref name="1yrtndr08">{{Cite web |title=Packers re-sign Bigby |url=http://blogs.jsonline.com/packers/archive/2008/03/21/packers-re-sign-bigby.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080324175359/http://blogs.jsonline.com/packers/archive/2008/03/21/packers-re-sign-bigby.aspx |archive-date=March 24, 2008 |access-date=March 21, 2008 |publisher=JSOnline.com}}</ref>

Bigby recorded the Packers’ first interception of the 2008 season in the opener against the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', picking off [[quarterback]] [[Tarvaris Jackson]] in the fourth quarter. He played in just seven games during the season due to injuries and was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]] with a shoulder injury on December 18. Bigby finished the 2008 season with 21 tackles, two pass deflections, and an interception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atari Bigby 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BigbAt20/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Bigby won his first Super Bowl when the Packers defeated the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in [[Super Bowl XLV]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLV - Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Green Bay Packers - February 6th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201102060pit.htm |access-date=2024-03-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was the first player to emerge from the tunnel when the Packers were introduced.

===Seattle Seahawks===
Bigby signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on August 16, 2011, and played in 15 regular season games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atari Bigby 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BigbAt20/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=2024-03-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
Bigby signed with the [[San Diego Chargers]] on March 16, 2012.<ref name="g460">{{cite web | last=Silva | first=Evan | title=Chargers sign Atari Bigby to two-year contract | website=NBC Sports | date=2012-03-16 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chargers-sign-atari-bigby-to-two-year-4-5-million-contract | access-date=2025-01-01}}</ref>

'''Arthur Gene Owens''' (born January 14, 1953) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]], [[kick returner|return specialist]], and [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. He was also a [[Track and field|track runner]] for the Mountaineers. Owens also played professionally in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL).

==Early life==
Owens moved from [[Alabama]] to [[Pennsylvania]] as a youth. As a senior, he led the [[Stroudsburg High School]] Mountaineers to an 11-0 record and established Pennsylvania records for touchdowns, with 41, and yards rushing, with 2,061. He was named a [[Kodak]] [[All-American]], [[United Press International|UPI]] and [[Associated Press|AP]] all-state, all-Big 33, all-Lehigh Valley and all-Eastern Pennsylvania for Coach Fred Ross. Owens also was on the Mounties' [[basketball]] and [[Track and field|track]] teams, and once ran the [[100-yard dash]] in 9.8 seconds.

==College career==
===Football===
Owens arrived at [[West Virginia University]] in 1972. He saw limited time as a freshman, only rushing for 72 yards and one touchdown. He also had 369 return yards, along with an 85-yard kick return.

As a sophomore in 1973, Owens was the projected [[Starting lineup|starter]] at the beginning of the season. But an injury led to newcomer [[Dwayne Woods]] to assume to role for the rest of the season. Owens only rushed for 391 yards and 3 touchdowns, but he did have 291 return yards with a kick return touchdown of 95 yards against [[Penn State]]. His sophomore season marked his final season of [[punt returner|returning punts]].

In his junior season of 1974, Owens went injury-free as he finally started through a whole season. His stats showed as well, as he rushed for a career-high 1,130 yards and 7 touchdowns, including an 85-yard run. He also had 301 kick returns yards, including a 73-yard return.

In his final season as a Mountaineer, 1975, Owens rushed for 1,055 yards and 5 touchdowns, with a 6.6 yards per carry average. He had a career-low 213 kick return yards, but a career-high 125 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.

Owens rushed for a then-school record 2,648 yards (now fourth on the career list), and set a record for career all-purpose rushing yardage with 3,971 yards (now third on the career list). His 6.4 career average for yards per carry is one of the best averages in school history and his 13 career 100-yard rushing games was a school record as well. After playing four seasons, Owens' 95-yard kick return for a touchdown as a junior was third-longest in school history. He received his degree at WVU in 2004.

===Track===
As a freshman, Owens tied a 41-year-old WVU record for the 100 yard dash by clocking a 9.6. He later bettered that mark with a 9.5, a record he shares with fellow two-sport star [[Harry Blake]]. Owens and Blake also teamed to set Mountaineer records in the 440- and 880-yard relays, and three times won the prestigious [[Penn Relays]]. [http://www.wvu.edu/~sports/hall_fame/artie_owens.htm]

==Professional career==
===San Diego Chargers===
Owens was selected in the fourth round of the [[1976 NFL draft]] by the [[San Diego Chargers]] as a [[wide receiver|receiver]] rather than a [[running back]]. Owens played with the Chargers for four seasons.

He started his pro career out in [[1976 NFL season|1976]], playing in 14 games. Although seeing some playing time, Owens only recorded 54 yards on three catches, along with one touchdown. In [[1977 NFL season|1977]], Owens saw no time at receiver, but did have one rush for three yards.

===After San Diego===

Following his season in 1979, Owens was picked up by the [[Buffalo Bills]]. He saw no action in [[1980 NFL season|1980]] with the Bills, and four games into the season he was traded to the [[New Orleans Saints]]. Owens saw no action with the 1-15 Saints either, and eventually retired after only 3 games in [[New Orleans, Louisiana|New Orleans]].

===USFL===

Three years after retiring from the NFL, Owens returned to professional football in [[1983 in sports|1983]]. He played for the [[Philadelphia/Baltimore Stars|Philadelphia Stars]] in the USFL for one season, before retiring from [[American football|football]] for good.

==Personal life==

Owens moved back to [[Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania|Stroudsburg]], where he instructed an alternative school for the mentally handicapped. He also assumed coaching roles at Stroudsburg High School, leading the school's [[1984 in sports|1984]] team to an undefeated season.

Owens attempted construction work in 1986, and after he finished it in 1987, he returned to his mental health profession. He currently works preparing mentally handicapped adults for their future lives. [http://www.wvu.edu/~sports/hall_fame/artie_owens.htm]

Good Guy? : Chargers: Once an interviewer's nightmare, the tight end now saves his meanness for the football field. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-07-26-sp-111-story.html |accessdate=2 May 2019 |agency=Los Angeles Times |date=July 26, 1991}} In [[1991 National Football League season|1991]], he lost his starter role, and was limited to playing in [[List of formations in American football|formations]] utilizing three tight ends. With the imminent reactivation of rookie tight end [[Duane Young]] from the [[injured reserve list]], the Chargers released Cox on October 29.{{cite news |last1=McKibben |first1=Dave |title=Chargers Release Veteran End Cox : NFL: Rookie Duane Young moves into starting spot. |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-10-30-sp-404-story.html |accessdate=2 May 2019 |date=October 30, 1991}} Cox subsequently was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]], but was waived on November 18, following two weeks of playing on special teams and goal line formations.{{cite news |last1=Mayo |first1=Michael |last2=Lazzarino |first2=Chris |title=BILLS LOSE BEEBE TO BROKEN COLLARBONE |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-1991-11-19-9102170565-story.html |accessdate=2 May 2019 |agency=Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel |date=November 18, 1991}} He was quickly signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]], for whom he played his last three NFL games.{{cite news |title=Browns sign three players |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1991/11/21/Browns-sign-three-players/3221690699600/ |accessdate=2 May 2019 |agency=UPI |date=November 21, 1991}} Cox had two children (Artesha and Ebonee){{cite web | last=Kline | first=Justin | title=Remembering Arthur Cox | website=Plant City Observer | date=2020-07-30 | url=https://www.plantcityobserver.com/remembering-arthur-cox/ | access-date=2025-03-28}}. Cox grew up in [[Plant City, Florida]], as one of 10 children. His father died when Cox was young. He died while suffering from kidney troubles.{{cite web | last=Kline | first=Justin | title=Remembering Arthur Cox | website=Plant City Observer | date=2020-07-30 | url=https://www.plantcityobserver.com/remembering-arthur-cox/ | access-date=2025-03-28}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Cox, Arthur}} [[Category:1961 births]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Plant City, Florida]] [[Category:Players of American football from Hillsborough County, Florida]] [[Category:American football tight ends]] [[Category:Texas Southern Tigers football players]] [[Category:Atlanta Falcons players]] [[Category:San Diego Chargers players]] [[Category:Cleveland Browns players]] [[Category:Miami Dolphins players]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:2020 deaths]] {{tightend-1960s-stub}}

'''Arthur Brown Jr.''' (born June 17, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. Brown was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the second round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[New York Jets]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], and [[San Antonio Commanders]].

==Early life==
Brown was born in [[Wichita, Kansas]].  He attended [[Wichita East High School]] in Wichita, and played high school football for the Wichita East Blue Aces. As a sophomore and junior he was a consensus first-team Class 6A all-state selection and as a junior he was named to the ''[[Wichita Eagle]]'' "Second 11" all-state team.  Brown registered 154 tackles (111 solo) and 7 sacks as a sophomore starter at linebacker in 2005, but also rushed for 462 yards at fullback. As a junior, Brown had 158 tackles, eight sacks and an interception.

Brown attended the 2006 [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]] summer camp where he ran the [[40-yard dash]] in 4.68 seconds.<ref name="USAToday" /> He also had an impressive performance at the 2007 U.S. Army Combine, and announced in June 2007 that he would participate in the 2008 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://recruiting.scout.com/2/654658.html |title=Scout.com: No. 1 Headed to US Army Bowl |access-date=September 11, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070704131612/http://recruiting.scout.com/2/654658.html |archive-date=July 4, 2007 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

[[Pete Carroll]] said that Brown was the best linebacker that he had seen in seven years—referring to [[D. J. Williams (linebacker)|D. J. Williams]]—, while [[Bob Stoops]] predicted Brown would win the [[Dick Butkus Award]] two times.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/06/04/sports/football/04brown.html |title=A Linebacker's Legend Is Growing in Kansas |access-date=September 10, 2007 |author=Thayer Evans |date=June 4, 2007 |work=New York Times| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131113114700/http://www.nytimes.com/2007/06/04/sports/football/04brown.html| archive-date=November 13, 2013| url-status= live}}</ref>  Primarily because of the Brown brothers, [[ESPNU]] nationally televised a matchup between East and [[Dodge City High School]] on September 7, 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kansas.com/266/story/169175.html |title=Signs of the times: ESPNU hits Dodge |access-date=September 10, 2007 |author=Sean Purcell |date=September 8, 2007 |publisher=Wichita Eagle}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>  Following the 2007 season, ''[[USA Today]]'' recognized him as a high school All-American.

Brown was considered the top prospect to come out of Wichita since [[Barry Sanders]] and [[Kamerion Wimbley]].  In September 2007, Brown announced that the schools he planned to visit were [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[LSU Tigers football|Louisiana State]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]], [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami (FL)]], and [[USC Trojans football|Southern California]].<ref>[http://www.kansas.com/sports/updates/story/179151.html Kansas.com: East's Arthur Brown will visit Bama, LSU, UNC, Miami, USC]</ref> [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]], [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech]], [[Florida Gators football|Florida]], and [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]], whom he had already visited, were still on his list of ten.  Though some predicted Brown would ultimately choose Oklahoma,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/stories/2007/08/23/cfbstorylines_0826.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721191825/http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/stories/2007/08/23/cfbstorylines_0826.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 21, 2012 |title=Some college football storylines to watch |access-date=September 10, 2007 |author=Tony Barnhart, Jeff D'Alessio |date=August 23, 2007 |publisher=Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref> he eliminated OU along with Alabama, Georgia Tech, and Georgia in early November.<ref>[http://www.kansas.com/680/story/223782.html Arthur Brown drops OU from list]</ref> On December 5, he eliminated Kansas State from his list.<ref>[http://www.kansas.com/sports/updates/story/246767.html East LB Arthur Brown eliminates K-State from possibilities]</ref> Brown was down to Louisiana State, North Carolina, Miami (FL), Southern California, and Florida, but with no clear front runner, when he held a press conference on December 17 at the Kansas Hall of Fame to announce his decision.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://recruiting.scout.com/2/687477.html |title=Scout.com Spreatsheet Data |access-date=October 6, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716021803/http://recruiting.scout.com/2/687477.html |archive-date=July 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> He decided to attend the University of Miami.

==College career==
Brown initially attended the [[University of Miami]], and played for the [[Miami Hurricanes football]] team. He struggled during his freshman year despite being Miami's top-rated recruit. Hurricanes coach [[Randy Shannon]] decided to move Brown from weakside to inside linebacker for his sophomore season, saying he began flourishing in the new role toward the end of the 2008 season. "The last two weeks of the season he was phenomenal at middle linebacker on scout team.  Like [[Ray Lewis (American football)|Ray Lewis]], when he first got here he was outside and he wasn't very good," said Shannon.<ref>[http://blogs.sun-sentinel.com/sports_college_hurricanes/2009/02/randy-shannon-talks-about-brown-.html Randy Shannon talks about Brown] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090222041702/http://blogs.sun-sentinel.com/sports_college_hurricanes/2009/02/randy-shannon-talks-about-brown-.html |date=February 22, 2009 }}</ref>

Brown left the Miami program in February 2010.<ref name="Navarro Miami Herald">{{Citation |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/colleges/um/story/1459302.html |title=Miami Hurricanes linebacker Arthur Brown returns to Kansas |newspaper=[[Miami Herald]] |date=February 2, 2010 |first=Manny |last=Navarro }}.</ref> Brown, along with his brother Bryce, were named in a report from [[Yahoo! Sports]] alleging that student-athletes, coaches and administrators were aware and received impermissible benefits from ex-booster and convicted felon [[Nevin Shapiro]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/investigations/news;_ylt=At7d5FJPpQojnULx7yaxb7Q5nYcB?slug=cr-renegade_miami_booster_details_illicit_benefits_081611 |work=Yahoo! Sports |title=Renegade Miami football booster spells out illicit benefits to players |date=August 16, 2011 |first=Charles |last=Robinson }}</ref>

He subsequently enrolled at [[Kansas State University]] in May 2010, and became a member of the [[Kansas State Wildcats football]] team.<ref>{{Citation|url=http://blogs.kansas.com/kstated/2010/03/02/arthur-brown-to-enroll-at-kansas-state/ |title=Arthur Brown to enroll at Kansas State |newspaper=The Wichita Eagle |date=March 2, 2010 |first=Kellis |last=Robinett |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721185759/http://blogs.kansas.com/kstated/2010/03/02/arthur-brown-to-enroll-at-kansas-state/ |archive-date=July 21, 2011 }}.</ref>  Brown's first season at Kansas State was very productive as he had 95 tackles, 2 sacks and 1 interception. Brown also contributed some key plays during the Wildcats 10–2 season, one such play included getting an interception off Heisman winning quarterback [[Robert Griffin III]] to set up game-winning field goal as the Wildcats beat [[2011 Baylor Bears football team|#15 Baylor Bears]]. He was the first player last season to pick Griffin, ending his streak at 110 passing attempts.<ref>{{cite web | last=McGuire | first=Corbin | title=K-State's Brown making most of time remaining | website=The Topeka Capital-Journal | date=2012-10-24 | url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/2012/10/24/k-states-brown-making-most-time-remaining/16417638007/ | access-date=2025-08-02}}</ref> Brown also had a 12 tackle game beating the [[2012 Iowa State Cyclones football team|Iowa State Cyclones]] as Kansas State finished the regular season 10–2. Brown was named Big 12 newcomer of the year, becoming the tenth Wildcat to do so and the fourth in the past five years.

In the 2012 season, Brown won the 2012 Big 12 Conference Defensive Player of the Year award, after registering 91 tackles, 2 interceptions (one was returned for a touchdown), six tackles for loss and one sack. He is the third Kansas State player to win the defensive player of the year award as named by the conference, after [[Mark Simoneau]] in 1999, and [[Terence Newman]] in 2002.

In the May 2022, Kansas State announced Arthur Brown would be inducted into the Ring of Honor.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://cjonline.com/story/sports/college/cat-zone/2022/05/18/kansas-state-football-enshrine-six-players-ring-honor/9829440002/ | title=Six all-time Kansas State football greats chosen for induction into Ring of Honor }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kstatesports.com/news/2022/5/18/k-state-unveils-six-member-ring-of-honor-class-of-2022.aspx#:~:text=The%20class%2C%20which%20will%20be,2011%2D14)%20and%20quarterback%20Ell | title=K-State Unveils Six-Member Ring of Honor Class of 2022 }}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Projected a second-round selection, Brown was ranked as the No. 4 outside linebacker available in the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/2013/OLB|title=2022 NFL Draft Prospect - Position Rankings}}</ref> He is compared to [[Daryl Washington]], because "neither linebacker has the ideal size for their position, but they compensate with sideline-to-sideline speed".<ref name="AZ Bust">[http://www.azcentral.com/sports/colleges/articles/20121229bust-miami-kansas-states-arthur-brown-star-home-state.html Bust in Miami, Kansas State’s Arthur Brown a star in home state]</ref> In the 2013 NFL Draft, the [[Baltimore Ravens]] picked Brown after their star middle linebacker [[Ray Lewis]] retired.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Brown underwent hernia surgery during the off-season a few weeks following the draft. Arthur was placed on injured reserve on January 1, 2015. On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Trim 2016 Roster to 53 Players|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Trim-2016-Roster-To-53-Players/996d3b0a-7452-413d-a887-9e94be344117|last=Downing|first=Garrett|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 3, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903074419/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Trim-2016-Roster-To-53-Players/996d3b0a-7452-413d-a887-9e94be344117|archive-date=September 3, 2017}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] claimed Brown off waivers on September 4, 2016.<ref>{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/09/04/jaguars-claim-marqueston-huff-arthur-brown/|title=Jaguars claim Marqueston Huff, Arthur Brown|first=Josh|last=Alper|date=September 4, 2016|access-date=September 5, 2016}}</ref> He was released by the Jaguars on December 6, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars Waive LB Arthur Brown, Promote LB Sean Porter|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/jaguars-waive-lb-arthur-brown-promote-lb-sean-porter/|date=December 6, 2016}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Brown was claimed off waivers by the Jets on December 7, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Acquire LB Arthur Brown on Waivers|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Acquire-LB-Arthur-Brown-on-Waivers/b7d8b6bf-1ca5-47ae-8513-063ceab65581?campaign=tw|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 7, 2016}}</ref> He was released on December 19, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign LB Randell Johnson|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Sign-LB-Randell-Johnson/7aa48ab1-6ed9-4027-bffb-d4f7a84fad00|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On March 17, 2017, Brown signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Linebacker Arthur Brown|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/03/17/seahawks-sign-linebacker-arthur-brown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318031003/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/03/17/seahawks-sign-linebacker-arthur-brown|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 18, 2017|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=March 17, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on July 31, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Linebacker Mike Morgan, Waive LB Arthur Brown|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/07/31/seahawks-sign-linebacker-mike-morgan-waive-lb-arthur-brown|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=July 31, 2017|access-date=August 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801003640/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/07/31/seahawks-sign-linebacker-mike-morgan-waive-lb-arthur-brown|archive-date=August 1, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===San Antonio Commanders===
On January 4, 2019, Brown signed with the [[San Antonio Commanders]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]]. On January 30, 2019, he was released by the Commanders as part of the final training camp cuts.

==Personal life==
Arthur is the son of Arthur Brown, Sr. and Lelonnie Brown. His uncle [[Lawrence Pete]] is a former [[Detroit Lions]] player,<ref name="NYT" /> while his younger brother [[Bryce Brown|Bryce]] is a former NFL [[running back]].

According to Jeremy Crabtree of ''[[Rivals.com]]'', the Browns were the first brothers ever to both be ranked five-star recruits.<ref name="USAToday">{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/football/2007-09-06-Browns_N.htm |title=Wichita gems hail from same team ... and family |access-date=September 10, 2007 |author=Steve Wieberg |date=September 6, 2007 |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

'''Atnaf DeShawn Harris''' (born February 27, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]] and [[Cal State Northridge Matadors football|Cal State Northridge Matadors]].

In his career, Harris played in the NFL for the [[Houston Texans]], [[Denver Broncos]], and with the [[San Jose SaberCats]], and [[Arizona Rattlers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL).

==Early life==
Harris attended [[Edison High School (Fresno, California)|Edison High School]] where he recorded 34 [[Reception (American football)|receptions]] for 667 yards and six [[touchdown]]s as a [[Twelfth grade|senior]]. He earned First-team All-North Yosemite League honors and named to the ''[[Fresno Bee]]'''s All-Star team.

==College career==
Harris played three seasons at Fresno State, where he recorded 26 receptions for 285 yards and four touchdowns in 23 games. He recorded 17 receptions 198 yards and three touchdowns as a freshman. He was a teammate of [[Rodney Wright]], future [[San Jose SaberCats]] teammate, for three seasons. He transferred to [[Cal State-Northridge]] for his senior season but the school dropped their football program that year. He then went back to Fresno State where he graduated with a degree in [[Sociology]].

==Professional career==

===NFL draft===
Harris was not expected to get [[Draft (sports)|drafted]] in the NFL, which he [[Undrafted sportsperson|was not]]. However, he did get attention from some pro scouts that were at the Fresno State pro day to watch [[quarterback]] [[David Carr (American football)|David Carr]], who was chosen first overall by the expansion [[Houston Texans]], by running a 4.42 [[40-yard dash]] and a vertical jump of 43.5".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kffl.com/article.php/259/123?printarticle=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050221130407/http://www.kffl.com/article.php/259/123?printarticle=1 |archive-date=2005-02-21 |last=Bonini |first= Ryan R. |title= NFL Draft Notebook – Draft Tidbits |work=KFFL.com |date=2002-03-26 |access-date=2008-09-12}}</ref>

===National Football League (2002–2004)===
After going undrafted in the [[2002 NFL draft]], Harris was signed by the Houston Texans, who had drafted his college teammate Carr, on May 22. He spent time on the teams [[practice squad]] before being signed to the active roster in November. He played in one regular season game as a rookie, a start in the regular season finale, in which he recorded one receptions for eight yards. After was waived by the Texans in the final cuts before the [[2003 NFL season|2003 season]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/transactions/_/name/hou/houston-texans |title=Houston Texans Transactions – 2003 |work=ESPN.com |year=2003 |access-date=2008-09-12}}</ref> and was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] in December 2003. He then spent the season on the Broncos practice squad,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/team/transactions/_/name/den/denver-broncos |title=Denver Broncos Transactions – 2003 |work=ESPN.com |year=2003 |access-date=2008-09-12}}</ref> but was waived on August 21, 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/01/sports/transactions.html |title=Transactions – Football |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2004-09-01 |access-date=2008-09-12}}</ref>

===Arena Football League (2006–2008)===

====San Jose SaberCats (2006)====
Harris signed to the practice squad of the San Jose SaberCats of the [[Arena Football League]] on November 3, 2005, and did not play in any games that season.

====Arizona Rattlers (2007–2008)====
He then signed with the [[Arizona Rattlers]] after spending the [[2006 Arena Football League season|2006 season]] on the San Jose practice squad.

As a rookie in [[2007 Arizona Rattlers season|2007]], Harris played in eight games, starting three, and finished third on the team with 41 receptions and 595 yards and nine touchdowns. His 14.5 yards-per-catch average was first on the team, and was 11th on the Rattlers all-time single season list.

In [[2008 Arizona Rattlers season|2008]], Harris played in just two games, both against his former team, the SaberCats. He recorded six receptions for 111 yards and two touchdowns. He also had two tackles. He was released by the Rattlers after the season.

==Personal life==
Harris enjoys playing [[video games]] in his free time, his favorite being ''[[Madden NFL]]''. He hopes to pursue a career in coaching high school football. Harris is married and has two sons: Jalen and Kamar.

'''Artie Enlow Smith''' (born May 15, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] and was selected by the 49ers in the fifth round of the [[1993 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Smith attended [[Stillwater High School (Oklahoma)|Stillwater High School]], where he was a two-time All-state selection at [[defensive end]]. He also played [[tight end]] and [[defensive tackle]]. He was a two-time All-conference selection in [[basketball]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://static.espn.go.com/nfl/profiles/profile/2377.html | title=Artie Smith NFL profile | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

He accepted a football scholarship from [[Louisiana Tech University]]. As a senior, he finished with 81 tackles. He had 12 tackles against the [[University of Alabama]]. He had 9 tackles and blocked a [[field goal]] against the [[University of South Carolina]].

He also  participated in [[track & field|track]], where he was the [[Sun Belt Conference]] [[Discus throw]] champion as a junior in 1992.

==Professional career==
===San Francisco 49ers===
Smith was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fifth round (116th overall) of the [[1993 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he played in 9 games and started in 2 at [[defensive end|right defensive end]]. On September 15, [[1994 NFL season|1994]], he was part of the cuts made after 2 games, to make room to sign [[Deion Sanders]] and [[Charles Mann (American football)|Charles Mann]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 September 1994 |title=Sanders signs up for the ring |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1955&dat=19940916&id=LYlVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Wj8NAAAAIBAJ&pg=3823,136206&hl=es |access-date=February 19, 2018 |website=Reading Eagle|via=Google News}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On September 16, [[1994 NFL season|1994]], Smith was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and played in 7 games as a reserve [[defensive end]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/09/17/sports/transactions-269883.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=17 September 1994 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> In [[1995 NFL season|1995]], he was a starter at [[defensive end|right defensive end]], [[defensive tackle|right defensive tackle]] and [[defensive tackle|left defensive tackle]], registering 44 tackles and 2 sacks.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19960504&id=SYwyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=COcFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4175,2983578&hl=es | title=Cincy extends lineman's pact | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> The next year, he played in 16 games (12 starts), while registering 34 tackles.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1876&dat=19970806&id=3rgeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=h88EAAAAIBAJ&pg=5606,2607132&hl=es | title=Bantering Thomas feeling jinxed by injuries | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was released on August 4, [[1997 NFL season|1997]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1755&dat=19970806&id=9yghAAAAIBAJ&sjid=W30EAAAAIBAJ&pg=2798,532393&hl=es | title=Around The Camps | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 11, [[1998 NFL season|1998]], he signed with the [[New England Patriots]] as a [[free agent]] after being out of football for a year.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1914&dat=19980312&id=T9ogAAAAIBAJ&sjid=UmsFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1480,1929558&hl=es | title=Sports Briefs | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was traded to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in exchange for future considerations on August 25.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/08/26/sports/nfl-transactions.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=26 August 1998 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
In [[1998 NFL season|1998]], he played a full season with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as a reserve [[defensive tackle]], posting 24 tackles, 7 quarterback pressures and one blocked [[field goal]].

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On April 22, [[1999 NFL season|1999]], he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=110&dat=19990423&id=tARQAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0FUDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2197,2318583&hl=es | title=Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 5.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/09/06/sports/transactions-380482.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=6 September 1999 | accessdate=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

'''Arthur Lee Whittington''' (September 4, 1955 – April 22, 2024) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU Mustangs]]. Selected in the seventh round of the [[1978 NFL draft]], Whittingham played in the NFL for five seasons with the [[Oakland Raiders]] and the [[Buffalo Bills]]. From 1983 to 1985, he played with the [[Oakland Invaders]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.usfl.info/invaders/roster.html |title=USFL.info - Oakland Invaders |access-date=2014-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120420055033/http://www.usfl.info/invaders/roster.html |archive-date=2012-04-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
As a rookie in 1978, Whittington proved to be a valuable weapon in the Raiders backfield. He finished the year with 661 yards rushing and seven scores while recording 23 catches for 106 yards over nine starts. The next season, he started just seven games but ran for 397 yards and two touchdowns while recording 19 catches for 240 yards. By 1980, Whittington had developed a complementary role, running for just 299 yards and 3 TD in two starts but had 19 catches for 205 yards.  His final year with Oakland, 1981, saw him start 2 games and run for 220 yards and one touchdown while recording 23 catches for 213 yards and 2 TD.

Along with being a serviceable running back, Whittington proved to be an adept kick returner. In 1978, he averaged 20.6 yards on 23 kick returns.  In 1980, he averaged 18.7 yards on 21 returns including 1 TD.  In 1981, he averaged 22.5 yards on 25 returns.

==Personal life==
Whittington had five children.<ref name=forman_04242024/> His two daughters Amber and Ashton are both [[YouTube personalities]].{{Citation needed|date=April 2024}} He was also the uncle of [[Jordan Whittington]], a former receiver for the University of Texas and 2024 sixth round draft pick of the [[Los Angeles Rams]]. He died of cancer in [[Houston]] on April 22, 2024, at the age of 68.<ref name=forman_04242024>{{cite news |first=Mike|last=Forman|title=Former Cuero, Super Bowl champion running back Arthur Whittington dies at 68 |date=April 22, 2024|url=https://www.victoriaadvocate.com/advosports/former-cuero-super-bowl-champion-running-back-arthur-whittington-dies-at-68/article_4124adf6-00f5-11ef-bcc9-d74d8694fb83.html |url-access=subscription|access-date=April 24, 2024 |newspaper=Victoria Advocate}}</ref>

'''Arthur Willis Jones III'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adeolu |first=Andrew |date=October 3, 2025 |title=Baltimore Ravens Super Bowl champion Arthur Jones III dies at 39 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/baltimore/news/baltimore-ravens-super-bowl-champion-arthur-willis-jones-iii-dies/ |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=CBS News}}</ref> (June 3, 1986 – October 3, 2025) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]]. He was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fifth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] and won [[Super Bowl XLVII]] with them. Jones also played for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Washington Redskins]]. He was also the older brother of former [[Ultimate Fighting Championship|UFC]] light heavyweight and heavyweight champion [[Jon Jones]] and defensive end [[Chandler Jones]].

==Early life==
Jones was born in [[Rochester, New York]], on June 3, 1986, to Arthur and Camille Jones.<ref name=nyt /> After moving to [[Endicott, New York|Endicott]], Jones attended [[Union–Endicott High School]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Art and Chandler Jones Target New Football Operations Center With Gift to Syracuse Athletics |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2022/10/13/art-and-chandler-jones-target-new-football-operations-center-with-gift-to-syracuse-athletics/ |access-date=October 15, 2022 |work=Syracuse University News |date=October 13, 2022}}</ref> At Union–Endicott he was on both the football and wrestling teams. He was a two time NY state champ in wrestling.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=March 19, 2014 |title='It's no secret': Arthur Jones says he can 'whoop' his UFC champ bro Jon Jones in a fight |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/its-no-secret-arthur-jones-says-he-can-whoop-his-ufc-champ-bro-jon-jones-in-a-fight |work=FOX Sports |access-date=October 3, 2025}}</ref> As a senior, he had 64 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], six [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], and one fumble recovery to help lead Union–Endicott to a Section IV championship. Following that championship season, Jones was ranked as the 18th best prospect in [[New York (state)|New York]] by ''SuperPrep''.<ref name="SU">{{cite web|url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6588&path=Football|title=#97 Arthur Jones|work=[[Syracuse University]]|access-date=August 9, 2009}}</ref>

Considered only a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Jones was not ranked among the nation's best defensive tackle prospects.<ref>{{Cite web |publisher=Rivals.com |title=Arthur Jones Profile |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=27679&sport=1 }}</ref> He chose Syracuse over [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]] and [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Mink |first=Nate |date=January 30, 2017 |title=10 most important recruits in Syracuse football history |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2017/01/10_most_important_recruits_in_syracuse_football_history.html |website=Syracuse.com |access-date=October 3, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
In 2005, as a [[true freshman]] at [[Syracuse University]], Jones was [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]].<ref name="Fumble">{{cite news|url=http://www.suathletics.com/sports/2006/11/11/2006FBgame10notes.aspx|title=Syracuse at South Florida|date=November 11, 2006|work=Suathletics.com|access-date=August 9, 2009}}</ref> Jones played more regularly in 2006. In a 34–14 win over [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami (Ohio)]], Jones [[quarterback sack|sacked]] their quarterback, [[Dan Raudabaugh|Daniel Raudabaugh]], for a loss of seven yards.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sports-att.espn.go.com/ncf/playbyplay?gameId=262660183&period=0|title=Miami (OH) 14, Syracuse 34|date=September 23, 2006|work=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=August 9, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605125639/http://sports-att.espn.go.com/ncf/playbyplay?gameId=262660183&period=0|archive-date=June 5, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 11, 2006, in a game at [[Raymond James Stadium]] home of the [[USF Bulls football|South Florida Bulls]], Jones recovered the first [[fumble]] of his collegiate career.<ref name="Fumble" /> In the same game he made five [[tackle (football move)|tackles]]. After playing in every game of the 2006 season, Jones had 15 tackles (including sacks) and one fumble recovery.<ref name="SU" />

The following year, against [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]], after Jones made a tackle on third [[Down (gridiron football)|down]], ''[[The Post-Standard|Post-Standard]]'' blogger and local radio host Brent Axe wrote, "Arthur Jones is having the game of his life right now."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.syracuse.com/axeman/index.ssf/2007/09/blogger_in_the_box_1st_half.html|title=Blogger in the Box|last=Axe|first=Brent|date=September 15, 2007|work=[[The Post-Standard]]|access-date=August 9, 2009}}</ref> As of October 21, 2007, Jones had five tackles for a loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.suathletics.com/sports/2007/10/21/fbpress102107.aspx|title=Head Coach Greg Robinson Press Conference (October 21, 2007)|date=October 21, 2007|work=Suathletics.com|access-date=August 9, 2009}}</ref> As of November 2, Jones had 14.5 tackles after the ball carrier crossed the line of scrimmage.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://rutgers.scout.com/a.z?s=183&p=2&c=697439|title=Pitt Looks To Get Back On Winning Track |last=Grdnic|first=Dale|date=November 2, 2007|work=[[Scout.com]]|access-date=August 10, 2009}}</ref> In the beginning of the second half against [[South Florida Bulls football|South Florida]] on November 11, Jones injured his ankle on a chop block.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.suathletics.com/sports/2007/11/18/fb_robinsontranscript_111807.aspx|title=Dantley makes first start; concedes some mental mistakes|last=Gelb|first=Matt|date=November 11, 2007|work=[[The Daily Orange]]|access-date=August 10, 2009}}</ref> On November 17, Jones was held out of the game against [[Connecticut Huskies football|Connecticut]] and according to coach [[Greg Robinson (American football coach)|Greg Robinson]] the decision came because, "Arthur has been too good of a football player for us to risk putting him out there and really getting him hurt."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.suathletics.com/sports/2007/11/18/fb_robinsontranscript_111807.aspx|title=Head Coach Greg Robinson Press Conference Transcript (November 18, 2007)|date=November 18, 2007|work=Suathletics.com|access-date=August 10, 2009}}</ref> For the season, he played in every game but the Connecticut game and was named second-team All-[[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East]]. His season high in tackles came against [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]] when he had nine.<ref name="SU" />

On September 10, 2008, against [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]], Jones had one sack and three tackles for a loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/scorecard/cfootballnews.asp?articleID=239762 |title=Penn State and Syracuse renew rivalry |date=September 10, 2008 |work=Seattle Post-Intelligencer |access-date=August 10, 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> After one month, Jones had four sacks to be one of the leaders for the Orange.<ref>{{cite news |last=Grdnic |first=Dale |date=September 27, 2008 |title=Temple of Doom |url=http://rutgers.scout.com/a.z?s=183&p=2&c=794989 |work=Scout.com |access-date=August 10, 2009}}</ref> After the [[2008 Syracuse Orange football team|2008 season]], Jones was named to the first-team All-Big East Conference and was an [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] candidate.<ref name="bigeast">{{cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=92485&SPID=11215&DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=3631151 |title=BIG EAST Announces 2008 Postseason Football Honors |work=Bigeast.com |date=December 10, 2008 |access-date=August 9, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090508115858/http://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=92485&SPID=11215&DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=3631151 |archive-date=May 8, 2009 }}</ref> Jones was one of only 10 players on the team to start every game. His season high in tackles came against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]] when he had eight. Following Syracuse's upset win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]] he was named Big East Defensive Player of the Week and was also awarded an [[ESPN]] ''Helmet Sticker'' for his performance. He ranks sixth on the Orange career record list for tackles for loss.<ref name="SU" />

In 2009, Jones missed three games, playing in nine and made 19 tackles (7 for losses) and 1.5 sacks and recovered 2 fumbles and was named first-team All-Big East for the second consecutive season.<ref name="SU" />

===Baltimore Ravens===
Jones was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fifth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] with the 157th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=February 23, 2019}}</ref> He was signed to a three-year deal on June 21, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/blog/2010/06/ravens_reach_agreement_with_dt_arthur_jones.html |title=Ravens reach agreement with DT Arthur Jones |work=Baltimore Sun |date=June 21, 2010 |access-date=July 16, 2010 |archive-date=September 1, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100901051315/http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/blog/2010/06/ravens_reach_agreement_with_dt_arthur_jones.html |url-status=dead }}.</ref> During his rookie season, Jones he made a position switch from 4-3 defensive tackle to 3-4 defensive end. He played 2 games without a single stat.<ref name=pfr/> Jones saw an increased role in the 2011 season by playing 14 games with one start, making 20 tackles.<ref name=pfr/> During the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]], Jones had 4.5 sacks in the regular season.<ref name=pfr/> The Ravens advanced to [[Super Bowl XLVII]] for the second time in franchise history against the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. In that game, Jones registered one fumble recovery as well as a key [[Quarterback sack|sack]] of 49ers quarterback [[Colin Kaepernick]].<ref name=nyt/> The Ravens ended up winning the game 34–31, earning Jones his first and only [[Super Bowl ring]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201302030sfo.htm |title=Super Bowl XLVII – San Francisco 49ers vs. Baltimore Ravens – February 3rd, 2013 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=November 8, 2017}}</ref> In 2013, Jones played 16 games (started 6) with 4.5 sacks on 27 solo tackles.<ref name=pfr/>

===Indianapolis Colts===
[[File:Arthur Jones (American football).JPG|thumb|Jones with the Colts in 2014]]

On March 11, 2014, Jones signed a 5-year contract with the Indianapolis Colts, worth more than $30 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/arthur-jones-indianapolis-colts-agree-on-five-year-deal-0ap2000000333046|title=Arthur Jones, Indianapolis Colts agree on five-year deal|last=Patra|first=Kevin|work=NFL.com|date=March 11, 2014|access-date=March 11, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24478388/report-former-ravens-dl-arthur-jones-signs-with-colts|title=Report: Former Ravens DL Arthur Jones signs with Colts|last=Wilson|first=Ryan|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 11, 2014|access-date=March 11, 2014}}</ref> During his first season with the Colts in 2014, Jones played 9 games (started 3) with 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble on 34 tackles.<ref name=pfr/> On September 5, 2015, Jones was placed on injured reserve for an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/colts-to-place-art-jones-on-season-ending-ir-0ap3000000522885|title=Colts to place Art Jones on season-ending IR|first=Conor|last=Orr|date=September 5, 2015|access-date=September 5, 2015}}</ref>

Jones was suspended the first four games of the 2016 season for violating the league's policy on performance enhancing drugs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arthur Jones apologizes for four-game PED suspension|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/arthur-jones-apologizes-for-four-game-ped-suspension-0ap3000000676291|author=Orr, Conor|website=NFL.com|date=July 26, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2016}}</ref> After returning from his suspension, Jones started all eight games he appeared in and tallied 30 tackles before being placed on injured reserve on December 19, 2016, with a groin injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arthur Jones Goes On Injured Reserve|url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Arthur-Jones-Goes-On-Injured-Reserve/6728e275-e449-4673-916c-149a3cbe7fcf|author=Bowen, Kevin|website=Colts.com|date=December 19, 2016|access-date=December 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327120920/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Arthur-Jones-Goes-On-Injured-Reserve/6728e275-e449-4673-916c-149a3cbe7fcf|archive-date=March 27, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 24, 2017, Jones was released by the Colts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2017/03/24/indianapolis-colts-release-dt-arthur-jones/|title=Indianapolis Colts Release DT Arthur Jones|website=Blogs.Colts.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=March 24, 2017|archive-date=March 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170325000357/http://blogs.colts.com/2017/03/24/indianapolis-colts-release-dt-arthur-jones/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Colts release defensive tackle Arthur Jones|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000795040/article/colts-release-defensive-tackle-arthur-jones|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170325140738/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000795040/article/colts-release-defensive-tackle-arthur-jones|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 25, 2017|publisher=NFL|access-date=March 24, 2017}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On November 1, 2017, Jones signed with the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign Defensive Lineman Arthur Jones|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Defensive-Lineman-Arthur-Jones/ac8cff51-aa4c-4e04-ad67-3755def002a5|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110154542/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Defensive-Lineman-Arthur-Jones/ac8cff51-aa4c-4e04-ad67-3755def002a5|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 10, 2017|author=Czarda, Stephen|website=Redskins.com|date=November 1, 2017}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 11, 2017, with a dislocated shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Promote Brandon Banks And Maurice Harris To Active Roster|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-promote-brandon-banks-and-maurice-harris-to-active-roster-19746211|author=Czarda, Stephen|website=Redskins.com|date=November 11, 2017}}</ref>

After the 2017 season ended, Jones announced his retirement via Instagram.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BddIPdPgY5C/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BddIPdPgY5C |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=limited|title=Instagram post by Arthur Jones • Jan 2, 2018 at 5:16pm UTC|website=Instagram|language=en|access-date=January 2, 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=Syracuse.com|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/index.ssf/2018/01/former_su_defensive_tackle_arthur_jones_retires_from_nfl.html|title=Former SU defensive tackle Arthur Jones retires from NFL|date=January 2, 2018|first=Ben |last=Burrows}}</ref>

'''Ashlee Palmer''' (born April 7, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]] and was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2009.

==College career==
On May 26, 2012, Palmer was inducted into the [[Compton Community College]] Athletics Hall of Fame, under the category of Football.

==Professional career==

===Buffalo Bills===
Palmer was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2009 NFL draft]] on May 1, 2009. He was waived on February 16, 2010.

===Detroit Lions===
Palmer was claimed off waivers by the [[Detroit Lions]] on February 18, 2010.

He was not re-signed by the Lions after the conclusion of the [[2014 NFL season]].

===New York Giants===
Palmer signed with the [[New York Giants]] on August 24, 2015. On September 5, 2015, the Giants cut Palmer.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 5, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925072219/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Arthur Moats''' (born March 14, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Buffalo Bills]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and [[Arizona Cardinals]]. He was selected by the Bills in the sixth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. Moats played [[college football]] for the [[James Madison Dukes football|James Madison Dukes]], where he was team captain.

In 2010, as a member of the Bills, Moats delivered the hit on [[Minnesota Vikings]] quarterback [[Brett Favre]] that ultimately led to the end of Favre's NFL record streak of consecutive starts the following week at 297.<ref name="buffalorumblings.com">{{Cite web |last=Galliford |first=Brian |date=2010-12-13 |title=Arthur Moats Officially Ends Brett Favre's Consecutive Games Played Streak |url=https://www.buffalorumblings.com/2010/12/13/1874484/arthur-moats-officially-ends-brett-favres-consecutive-games-played |access-date=2025-07-20 |website=Buffalo Rumblings |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

Moats hosts a football podcast, ''The Arthur Moats Experience With Deke.''

==Early life==
Moats was born in [[Norfolk, Virginia]], and was raised in [[Portsmouth, Virginia]], where he attended [[Churchland High School]] and graduated in 2006. He graduated from [[James Madison University]] with a degree in [[political science]]. Moats is currently in his second year of earning his master's degree online, saying he values education greatly. His father is a former marine and current high school math teacher.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/10-Questions-With-Arthur-Moats/5a5aca0d-7981-46c8-a595-ed09bca74544|title=10 Questions With Arthur Moats|publisher=|access-date=November 16, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141117060541/http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/10-Questions-With-Arthur-Moats/5a5aca0d-7981-46c8-a595-ed09bca74544|archive-date=November 17, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Moats finished his career at [[James Madison University]] with 208 tackles. He played in all of his team's games as a true freshman. He started only 5 games as a sophomore, but became a full-time starter for his junior and senior years. Moats won the 2009 [[Buck Buchanan Award]] as the top [[Division I (NCAA)#Football Championship Subdivision|FCS]] defensive player.<ref>{{cite news|title=Arthur Moats captures 2009 Buck Buchanan Award |publisher=The Sports Network |access-date=April 25, 2010 |url=http://www.sportsnetwork.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=sportsnetwork&page=cfoot2/misc/2009buchanan_moats_815.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110404060312/http://www.sportsnetwork.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=sportsnetwork&page=cfoot2%2Fmisc%2F2009buchanan_moats_815.htm |archive-date=April 4, 2011 }}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
Moats was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the sixth round, 178th overall, in the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He is the only [[Buck Buchanan Award]] winner to be drafted by the Bills. In the Bills [[3-4 defense|3-4 defensive]] scheme, he moved from [[defensive end]] to [[inside linebacker]], which is an unusual position change considering most defensive ends move to [[outside linebacker]] in 3-4 defensive schemes.  After several weeks of failing to generate a consistent pass rush, Bills head coach [[Chan Gailey]] decided to move Moats to his more natural position of outside linebacker to utilize his pass rushing skill set.

In a Week 13 contest of the 2010 season, Moats delivered a hit on [[Minnesota Vikings]] [[quarterback]] [[Brett Favre]] that aggravated the quarterback's shoulder injury. It was Moats' hit that eventually led to Favre's consecutive starts streak ending at 297 when he did not play against the [[New York Giants]] the following week.<ref name="buffalorumblings.com" />

Moats' personal catch phrase, 'Don't Cross The Moats', was created by Joe Zogaib. Since then, it has a become a popular trending topic on Twitter, and Moats himself even tattooed the phrase across his upper back.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://paranoiadaily.com/sports/time-to-billieve-once-again/attachment/moats-tat2/ |title=Moats-tat2 |access-date=September 6, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331191836/http://paranoiadaily.com/sports/time-to-billieve-once-again/attachment/moats-tat2/ |archive-date=March 31, 2012 }}</ref>

In December 2013, Moats was named the team's [[Walter Payton Man of the Year]] for 2013. Moats earned this honor through his work with the United Way of Buffalo and Erie County and other local groups. Moats was also named the Bills Ed Block Courage Award recipient. He earned this honor by overcoming adversity from an injury and exemplifying courage both on and off the field.<ref>{{cite web|title=Moats selected as Bills Ed Block Courage Award recipient|url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Moats-selected-as-Bills-Ed-Block-Courage-Award-recipient/349a9bec-b011-48cd-a6b4-04219df39ffd|access-date=April 2, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403095942/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Moats-selected-as-Bills-Ed-Block-Courage-Award-recipient/349a9bec-b011-48cd-a6b4-04219df39ffd|archive-date=April 3, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also conducts numerous school visits and takes part in the NFL Play 60 initiative.<ref>{{cite web|title=Buffalo Bills' Arthur Moats Named Team's Man of the Year|url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/buffalobills/2013/12/14/buffalo-bills-arthur-moats-named-teams-man-of-the-year/}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On March 24, 2014, the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] signed Moats to a one-year, $795,000 contract with a signing bonus of $65,000.<ref name="sportrac">{{cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/pittsburgh-steelers/arthur-moats-6686/| title=Sportrac.com: Arthur Moats contracts| access-date=December 19, 2016| website=sportrac.com}}</ref><ref>[http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/24/steelers-sign-arthur-moats/ Steelers sign Arthur Moats]. ''ProFootballTalk.com''. Retrieved March 24, 2014.</ref> He began his first season with the Pittsburgh Steelers as the backup right outside linebacker behind [[Jarvis Jones]]. In the season opener against the [[2014 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]], he assisted in one tackle during his Steelers debut as they won 30-27. On September 21, 2014, Moats made two solo tackles and sacked Panthers quarterback [[Cam Newton]] as the Steelers routed the [[2014 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] 37-19. The next game, he got his first start with the Steelers in place of an injured Jarvis Jones and made one solo tackle in a 24-27 loss to the [[2014 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In Week 9, Moats collected three combined tackles, sacked Ravens quarterback [[Joe Flacco]], and forced a fumble as Pittsburgh defeated the [[2014 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] 43-23. The following week, he made a season-high four combined tackles in a 13-20 loss to the [[2014 New York Jets season|New York Jets]]. He finished the season with 23 combined tackles, four sacks, and two forced fumbles while appearing in all 16 regular season contests and starting ten.

On March 9, 2015, the Pittsburgh Steelers signed Moats to a three-year, $7.50 million contract with a signing bonus of $1.90 million.<ref name="sportrac"/><ref>[http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-agree-to-terms-with-Arthur-Moats/fbe8ef0a-46d0-4022-ad9d-58c2743dcebd/ Steelers agree to terms with Arthur Moats] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150311102417/http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-Agree-to-Terms-with-Arthur-Moats/fbe8ef0a-46d0-4022-ad9d-58c2743dcebd |date=March 11, 2015 }}. ''Steelers.com''. Retrieved March 9, 2015.</ref> Moats began 2015 as the left outside linebacker ahead of rookie [[Bud Dupree]]. In the second game of the season, he made three combined tackles and was credited with half a sack after taking down [[2015 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] quarterback [[Colin Kaepernick]] while helping his team rout the 49ers 43-18. On January 3, 2016, Moats racked up a season-high six solo tackles and sacked [[2015 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] quarterback [[Austin Davis (American football)|Austin Davis]], helping the Steelers win 28-12. On January 9, 2016, he collected five combined tackles as the Steelers defeated the [[2015 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] 18-16 in an AFC Wild-card matchup. Moats finished the 2015 season with 35 combined tackles, four sacks, and two pass deflections and appeared in all 16 games and started 11.

Moats began the 2016 season as the backup left outside linebacker behind Bud Dupree. He started the season opener in place of an injured Dupree and made one tackle and a pass deflection in a 38-16 win over the [[2016 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]]. The next game, Moats collected three combined tackles and sacked [[2016 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] quarterback [[Andy Dalton]], helping the Steelers win 24-16. On November 20, 2016, Moats made two solo tackles and sacked [[2016 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] quarterback [[Josh McCown]] twice, as the Steelers defeated the Browns 24-9.

Throughout the first 12 games of the 2017 season, Moats played almost exclusively on special teams, with only 47 snaps on defense. Following injuries to [[Ryan Shazier]] and [[Tyler Matakevich]] on December 4 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Moats was moved to left inside linebacker, splitting time with [[Sean Spence]] and [[L. J. Fort]] for the Steelers' December 10 game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]].

===Arizona Cardinals===
On July 25, 2018, Moats signed a one-year contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Sign Arthur Moats, Jacquies Smith|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-linebacker-arthur-moats-defensive-end-jacquies-smith|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=July 26, 2018}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve with a sprained MCL on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Make Cuts To Reach 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-cuts-to-reach-53-man-roster-2018|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref> He was released on October 9, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals release Arthur Moats|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/10/09/cardinals-release-arthur-moats/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=October 9, 2018}}</ref>

On June 10, 2019 Moats officially announced his retirement from the [[NFL]] via Instagram and Twitter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/veteran-lb-arthur-moats-retiring-from-nfl/|title=Veteran LB Arthur Moats Retiring From NFL|author=Bouda, Nate|date=June 10, 2019}}</ref>
