The [[New York Jets]] selected Davis in the third round (68th overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2020/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-18 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The Jets previously traded defensive lineman [[Leonard Williams (defensive end)|Leonard Williams]] to the [[New York Giants]] to obtain the pick. He was the sixth safety drafted in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets select Ashtyn Davis with No. 68 pick in NFL Draft|url=https://nypost.com/2020/04/24/jets-select-ashtyn-davis-with-no-68-pick-in-nfl-draft/|first=Brian|last=Costello|work=[[New York Post]]|date=April 24, 2020|access-date=April 26, 2020}}</ref> He was the first of two Cal safeties drafted in 2020, along with [[Jaylinn Hawkins]] who was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the fourth round (132nd overall).

====2020 season====
{{see also|2020 New York Jets season}}
On July 24, 2020, the New York Jets signed Davis to a four–year, [[United States dollar|$]]4.91 million [[contract]] that included an initial [[signing bonus]] of $1.36 million.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web|title=Spotrac.com: Ashtyn Davis contract|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/47663/ashtyn-davis|access-date=January 30, 2025|website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> 

Davis entered [[training camp]] slated to be the starting nickelback and primary backup safety. On July 25, 2020, the New York Jets traded starting strong safety [[Jamal Adams]] to the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. Following his departure, Defensive coordinator [[Gregg Williams]] held a competition between David and [[Bradley McDougald]] for the starting role.<ref>{{cite web |title=Top 2020 NFL training camp battles for Jets: New York's loss of Jamal Adams could be Ashtyn Davis' gain |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/top-2020-nfl-training-camp-battles-for-jets-new-yorks-loss-of-jamal-adams-could-be-ashtyn-davis-gain/ |access-date=January 30, 2025 |website=cbssports.com |date=August 5, 2020 |author=Bryan DeArdo}}</ref> Head coach [[Adam Gase]] named Davis a backup safety, behind [[Marcus Maye]] and Bradley McDougald.<ref>{{cite web |title=NY Jets depth chart: Breaking down the 2020 roster, position-by-position |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nfl/jets/2020/09/09/ny-jets-depth-chart-position-position-breakdown-2020-roster/5755882002/ |access-date=January 30, 2025 |website=North Jersey.com}}</ref>

On September 13, 2020, Davis made his professional regular season debut and made one solo tackle during a 17–27 loss at the [[2020 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. The following week, Davis earned his first career start as the Jets lost 13–31 to the [[2020 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] in Week 2. He was inactive for two consecutive games (Weeks 3–4) after injuring his groin. Davis became the starting strong safety in Week 8 after Bradley McDougald underwent surgery after injuring his shoulder. On November 22, 2020, Davis had a team-leading 12 combined tackles (eight solo) and recovered a fumble on the goal line after teammate [[Marcus Maye]] caused wide receiver [[Keenan Allen]] to lose possession during a 34–28 loss at the [[2020 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers - November 22nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011220sdg.htm |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> On December 6, 2020, Davis recorded six combined tackles (five solo) before exiting in the third quarter due to an injury as the Jets lost 28–31 to the [[2020 Las Vegas Raiders season|Las Vegas Raiders]]. Om December 12, 2020, the New York Jets placed Davis on [[injured reserve]] for the remainder of the season due to a foot injury. He would remain inactive for the last four games of the regular season (Weeks 14–17).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=December 12, 2020 |title=Jets Activate CB Bless Austin, TE Trevon Wesco from Injured Reserve; Place 3 on IR |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-cb-bless-austin-te-trevon-wesco-from-injured-reserve-place-3-on-ir |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with 36 combined tackles (25 solo), one pass deflection, and a fumble recovery while appearing in ten games with five starts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pro-Football-Reference: Ashtyn Davis stats (2020) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviAs00.htm |access-date=January 30, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

====2021 season====
{{see also|2021 New York Jets season}}
On January 14, 2021, the [[New York Jets]] hired [[2020 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers']] defensive coordinator [[Robert Saleh]], replacing Adam Gase after the Jets finished the [[2020 NFL season]] 2-14.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-reach-agreement-with-robert-saleh-to-become-head-coach|title=Jets Reach Agreement in Principle with Robert Saleh to Become Head Coach deal|website=www.newyorkjets.com|last=Lange|first=Randy|date=January 14, 2020|access-date=January 14, 2020}}</ref> Davis missed the start of training camp as he was still recovering from his injury. Defensive coordinator [[Jeff Ulbrich]] named Marcus Maye and [[Lamarcus Joyner]] the starting safeties in his absence.<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 New York Jets Preview: Safeties |url=https://lastwordonsports.com/nfl/2021/08/15/2021-new-york-jets-preview-safeties/ |access-date=January 30, 2025 |website=laststopsports.com |date=August 15, 2021}}</ref>

Davis spent the entire pre-season on the [[Physically unable to perform|PUP list/Active]] as he recovered from his foot surgery. On September 1, 2021, the New York Jets placed Davis on injured reserve to begin the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Lange |first1=Randy |last2=Greenberg |first2=Ethan |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Jets Sign 3, Place 3 on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-3-place-3-on-injured-reserve |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> On October 2, 2021, the New York Jets activated Davis from injured reserve after missing the first three games (Weeks 1–3).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=October 2, 2021 |title=Jets Activate S Ashtyn Davis, S Sharrod Neasman |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-s-ashtyn-davis-s-sharrod-neasman |access-date=2023-09-29 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> During his absence, starting strong safety Lamarcus Joyner injured his elbow and was placed on injured reserve. In Week 5, Davis was appointed as the starting strong safety for the remainder of the season taking the starting role from [[Adrian Colbert]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign 4 Players; Place 4 on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-4-players-place-4-on-injured-reserve|last1=Greenberg|first1=Ethan|last2=Allen|first2=Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 14, 2021}}</ref> In Week 7, Davis collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (ten solo) as the Jets lost 13–54 at the [[2021 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. On December 19, 2021, Davis made eight combined tackles (three solo) and had his first career interception on a pass thrown by [[Tua Tagovailoa]] to tight end [[Mike Gesicki]] during a 24–31 loss at the [[2021 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Jets at Miami Dolphins - December 19th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112190mia.htm |access-date=January 30, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 24, 2021, the New York Jets placed Davis on the [[COVID-19|COVID-19/Reserve]] list and he was subsequently inactive for a Week 16 victory against the [[2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He finished the [[2021 NFL season]] with 62 combined tackles (43 solo), three pass deflections, two interceptions, and was credited with half a sack while appearing in 13 games with ten starts. He received an overall grade of 60.7 by Pro Football Focus, which ranked 44th out of 64 safeties and earned a coverage grade of 66.1 which ranked 34th amongst all safeties in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Should NY Jets fans have faith in Ashtyn Davis going into 2022? |url=https://jetsxfactor.com/2022/05/26/ny-jets-fans-ashtyn-davis-faith-2022/ |access-date=February 1, 2025 |website=jetsxfactor.com |date=May 26, 2022 |author=Stefan Steling}}</ref>

====2022 season====
{{see also|2022 New York Jets season}}
The job as the starting strong safety was available after Marcus Maye departed during free agency. Throughout training camp, Davis competed for the role against Lamarcus Joyner, [[Jason Pinnock]], [[Will Parks]], and [[Tony Adams (safety)|Tony Adams]].<ref>{{cite web |title=These 5 guys all have a shot to be the NY Jets' starting FS in 2022 |url=https://jetsxfactor.com/2022/05/28/ny-jets-starting-free-safety/ |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=JetsXFacror.com |author=David Wyatt-Hupton |date=May 28, 2022}}</ref> Head coach Robert Saleh named Davis as a backup free safety to start the season, behind starter [[Jordan Whitehead]] and starting strong safety Lamarcus Joyner.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Jets release first unofficial depth chart of 2022 |url=https://jetsxfactor.com/2022/08/08/new-york-jets-depth-chart-2022/ |access-date=January 31, 2025| website=JetsXFacror.com| author=Rivka Boord| date=August 8, 2022}}</ref> On September 18, 2022, Davis made one solo tackle, had his only pass break up of the season, and intercepted a pass by [[Jacoby Brissett]] to wide receiver [[Amari Cooper]] in the closing seconds to seal a 31–30 victory at the [[2022 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. He was inactive during a Week 7 victory at the [[2022 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] after injuring his hamstring. He re-aggravated his hamstring injury and subsequently was sidelined for two more games (Weeks 13–14). He was mainly limited to appearing on special teams in 2022 and only recorded three combined tackles (one solo), one pass deflection, and one interception in 14 games with no starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Ashtyn Davis stats (2022) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviAs00.htm |access-date=January 31, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

====2023 season====
{{see also|2023 New York Jets season}}
Lamarcus Joyner departed in free agency and was replaced by [[Chuck Clark]]. The starting free safety role was available after Clark to his ACL and was ruled out for the entire [[2023 NFL season]]. The New York Jets signed free agent [[Adrian Amos]] to compete for the job against Davis and Tony Adams.<ref>{{cite web| title=Dissecting the New York Jets' Biggest 2023 Roster Weaknesses: What are the New York Jets' plans at free safety after losing Chuck Clark?| url=https://lastwordonsports.com/nfl/2023/07/04/jets-biggest-roster-weakness-free-safety/ |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=lastwordonsports.com |date=July 4, 2023}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Jeff Ulbrich]] chose [[Tony Adams (safety)|Tony Adams]] and Jordan Whitehead to begin the season as the starting safeties, which pushed Davis into a backup safety.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads com: New York Jets depth chart (09/01/2023)| url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/275/NYJ |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On November 19, 2013, Davis broke up a pass attempt and intercepted a pass by [[Josh Allen]] and returned it for a career-high 51–yards during a 6–32 loss at the [[2023 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. In Week 15, he collected a season-high six combined tackles (four solo) as the Jets were routed 0–30 at the [[2023 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. In Week 18, Davis recorded five combined tackles (three solo), a season-high three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass attempt by [[Bailey Zappe]] during a 17–3 victory at the [[2023 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]]. He finished with 37 combined tackles (23 solo), eight pass deflections, three interceptions, and three fumble recoveries in 17 games and five starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Ashtyn Davis stats (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviAs00.htm |access-date=January 30, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Davis an overall grade of 74.7 in 2023.<ref>{{cite web| title=After Re-Signing With New York Jets Should Ashtyn Davis Be Starter?| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/New-York-ashtyn-davis-sign-contract-deserve-starter-safety |access-date=January 30, 2025| website=off.com |author=Nick Feria| date=April 12, 2024}}</ref>

====2024 season====
{{see also|2024 New York Jets season}}
On April 14, 2024, the New York Jets signed Davis to a one–year, $2.74 million contract that includes an initial signing bonus of $157,500.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pullano |first=John |date=April 11, 2024 |title=S Ashtyn Davis Re-Signs with Jets |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-ashtyn-davis-04-11-2024 |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> 
{{external media 
| video1 =
[https://www.newyorkjets.com/video/ashtyn-davis-interception-jets-vs-dolphins-highlight-week-18-2024 Ashtyn Davis INTs Tyler Huntley]
}}
Following the departure of Jordan Whitehead via free agency, head coach [[Robert Saleh]] stated there would be an open competition for both starting safety roles between Davis, Chuck Clark, and Tony Adams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets' biggest position battle for 2024 may be at an unexpected slot| url=https://empiresportsmedia.com/new-york-jets/jets-biggest-position-battle-for-2024-may-be-at-an-unexpected-slot/ |access-date=January 31, 2025| website=empiresportsmedia.com |author=Matthew Legros| date=June 17, 2024}}</ref> He began the regular season as a backup safety, behind starters Chuck Clark and Tony Adams.<ref>{{cite web| title=New York Jets release first depth chart of regular season| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/news/new-york-jets-release-first-depth-chart-regular-season |access-date=January 31, 2025| website=si.com| author=Matthew Postins| date=September 5, 2024}}</ref>

On October 8, 2024, the New York Jets fired head coach Robert Saleh after a 2–3 start and named defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich as the interim head coach. In Week 6, he racked up a season-high nine combined tackles (six solo) during a 20–23 loss at the [[2024 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. The following week, Davis recorded two solo tackles before suffering a head injury early in the fourth quarter and was removed from the Jets' 15–37 loss at the [[2024 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] in Week 7. He was diagnosed with a [[concussion]] and remained inactive in concussion protocol for the next two games (Weeks 8–9).<ref>{{cite web| title=Jets' Ashtyn Davis: Possible concussion| url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jets-ashtyn-davis-being-evaluated-for-concussion/ |access-date=January 31, 2025| website=cbssports.com |date=October 20, 2024}}</ref> On January 5, 2025, Davis earned his first and only start of the season after Chuck Clark tore his pectoral muscle and collected a season-high tying nine combined tackles (eight solo), a season-high two pass break ups, and a career-high two interceptions off passes thrown by [[Tyler Huntley]] during a 20–32 victory against the [[2024 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Miami Dolphins at New York Jets - January 5th, 2025| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202501050nyj.htm| access-date=January 31, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He finished the [[2024 NFL season]] with a total of 35 combined tackles (25 solo), two pass deflections, and two interceptions in 15 games and one start.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Ashtyn Davis stats (2024)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaviAs00.htm| access-date=January 31, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
====2025 season====
On March 13, 2025, Davis signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] on a one-year, $3 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-davis|title= Dolphins Sign Davis |work=Miami Dolphins|date=March 13, 2025}}</ref> Davis made 15 appearances (including 12 starts) for the Dolphins during the regular season, recording one interception, four pass deflections, one forced fumble, and 65 combined tackles.

===San Francisco 49ers===
====2026 season====
On June 2, 2026, Davis signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign Safety Ashtyn Davis to a One-Year Deal; Waive RB Jermar Jefferson|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-safety-ashtyn-davis-to-a-one-year-deal-waive-rb-jermar-jefferson|website=49ers.com|date=June 2, 2026|access-date=June 2, 2026}}</ref>

}}'''Asante Samuel Jr.''' (born October 3, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2018 |title=Asante Samuel, Jr. |url=https://seminoles.com/sports/football/roster/asante-samuel-jr/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513113824/https://seminoles.com/sports/football/roster/asante-samuel-jr/ |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=Florida State Seminoles |language=en-US}}</ref> and was selected by the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] in the second round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Jeff |date=May 1, 2021 |title=Chargers pick cornerback, receiver, tight end on Day 2 of NFL draft |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/chargers/story/2021-04-30/chargers-pick-cornerback-asante-samuel-jr-in-round-2-of-nfl-draft |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Samuel was born on October 3, 1999, in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel Jr. Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs00.htm |access-date=December 6, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> to [[Asante Samuel|Asante Samuel Sr.]] and Candice Doe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OSDB – Asante Samuel Jr. – Los Angeles Chargers |url=https://www.osdbsports.com/nfl/players/asante-samuel-jr/02b08a8b-a3bd-44d1-8930-e6f51b029a22 |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=OSDB – Online Sports Database}}</ref> Samuel credits his grandmother, Christine Samuel, for helping raise him and being an important person in his life.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Jeff |date=September 11, 2021 |title=Asante Samuel Jr. has trouble learning from one former NFL player — his dad |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/chargers/story/2021-09-11/asante-samuel-jr-chargers-nfl-career-father-relationship |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> When he was 14, his mother was diagnosed with a brain tumor,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Shelley |date=May 15, 2021 |title=Los Angeles Chargers second-rounder Asante Samuel Jr.'s inherited inspiration goes beyond famous father |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles-chargers/post/_/id/28246/chargers-second-rounder-asante-samuel-jr-s-bloodline-inspiration-goes-beyond-famous-father |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> from which she recovered after surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 26, 2020 |title=Asante Samuel Jr. |url=https://seminoles.com/asantesamueljr/ |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=Florida State Seminoles |language=en-US |archive-date=October 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221009145239/https://seminoles.com/asantesamueljr/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Samuel played [[high school football]] at [[St. Thomas Aquinas High School (Florida)|St. Thomas Aquinas]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Stephen |date=March 22, 2021 |title=Cleveland Browns, Potential NFL Draft Target: Asante Samuel, Jr |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/cleveland-browns/LongFormArticle/Cleveland-Browns-Potential-NFL-Draft-Target-Asante-Samuel-Jr-162757950/ |access-date=April 7, 2021 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> He was a four-star recruit coming out of high school and committed to [[Florida State University|Florida State]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel Jr., Florida State Seminoles, Cornerback |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Asante-Samuel-Jr-78738/ |access-date=July 13, 2020 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Furones |first=David |date=December 22, 2017 |title=Asante Samuel Jr. stays loyal to commitment, signs with FSU |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/fl-sp-early-signing-asante-samuel-20171222-story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171224034457/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/fl-sp-early-signing-asante-samuel-20171222-story.html |archive-date=December 24, 2017 |access-date=July 13, 2020 |website=South Florida Sun Sentinel }}</ref>

== College career ==
As a sophomore in 2019, Samuel was named to the [[2019 All-ACC football team|third-team All-ACC]] team after recording 48 tackles, one interception, and 14 pass breakups.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 3, 2019 |title=Clemson Leads 2019 All-ACC Football Team |url=http://theacc.com/news/2019/12/3/athlete-awards-clemson-leads-2019-all-acc-football-team.aspx |access-date=July 13, 2020 |website=The ACC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2018 |title=Asante Samuel, Jr. |url=https://seminoles.com/sports/football/roster/asante-samuel-jr/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513113824/https://seminoles.com/sports/football/roster/asante-samuel-jr/ |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |access-date=July 13, 2020 |website=Florida State Seminoles |language=en-US}}</ref> As a junior in 2020, he was named to the first-team All-ACC team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2020 |title=Tigers, Irish Lead All-ACC Football Team |url=http://theacc.com/news/2020/12/21/athlete-awards-tigers-irish-lead-all-acc-football-team.aspx |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=The ACC |language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
Samuel was selected by the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] in the second round (47th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayre |first=Chris |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Chargers Draft CB Asante Samuel Jr. With 47th Pick |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/asante-samuel-jr-nfl-draft-cornerback-florida-state |access-date=May 8, 2021 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref> On May 12, 2021, Samuel signed with the Chargers on a deal worth just over $7 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=May 12, 2021 |title=Chargers, Asante Samuel Jr. Agree to Deal |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/05/chargers-asante-samuel-jr-agree-to-deal#ref=home |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref> He recorded his first career interception in week 2 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Robinson |first=Logan |date=September 19, 2021 |title=WATCH: Asante Samuel Jr. records first NFL career interception |url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/football/asante-samuel-jr-interception |access-date=September 21, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He was [[Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week]] in back-to-back weeks, weeks 2 and 3.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Michael |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Asante Samuel Jr. named to list of 2nd-year players to rebound from injury in 2022 |url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2022/7/18/23268354/chargers-news-nfl-asante-samuel-jr-cbs-sports |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=Bolts From The Blue |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in and started 12 games. He finished with 43 total tackles (33 solo), two interceptions, and 11 passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Samuel recorded his first interception of the 2022 season in week 1 against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Las Vegas Raiders at Los Angeles Chargers – September 11th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209110sdg.htm |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2022 season, Samuel appeared in all 17 games and started 15. He finished with 57 total tackles (48 solo), two interceptions, and 11 passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2022–23 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 31, Los Angeles Chargers 30|Wild Card Round]] of the playoffs, Samuel recorded three interceptions in the first half in the team's 31–30 loss to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Los Angeles Chargers at Jacksonville Jaguars – January 14th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301140jax.htm |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |date=January 15, 2023 |title=2023 NFL playoffs: Chargers' Asante Samuel Jr. makes history in first half of wild-card game vs. Jaguars |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2023-nfl-playoffs-chargers-asante-samuel-jr-makes-history-in-first-half-of-wild-card-game-vs-jaguars/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2023 season, Samuel recorded 63 tackles, two interceptions, and 13 passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel Jr. 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SamuAs00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

After four games, Samuel was placed on [[injured reserve]] for a shoulder injury on October 12, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41757324/chargers-place-rb-gus-edwards-cb-asante-samuel-jr-ir|work=ESPN.com|title=Chargers place RB Gus Edwards, CB Asante Samuel Jr. on IR|first=Kris|last=Rhim|date=October 12, 2024|accessdate=January 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chargers/chargers-embattled-finally-breaks-silence-injury-asante-samuel|title=Chargers' embattled CB finally breaks silence about injury|first=Chris|last=Roling|work=SI.com|date=January 13, 2025|accessdate=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On November 12, 2025, the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] signed Samuel to their [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Varley|first=Teresa|title=Howard activated as Steelers make moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/howard-activated-as-steelers-make-moves|work=Steelers.com|accessdate=November 12, 2025|date=November 12, 2025}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make multiple roster moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-multiple-roster-moves-x8951|website=Steelers.com|date=December 2, 2025}}</ref> In a December 15 game against the [[2025 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]], his third game as a Steeler, Samuel intercepted a [[Tua Tagovailoa]] pass for his first interception in over two years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asante Samuel Jr. jumps route to snag INT on Tua |url=https://www.nfl.com/videos/asante-samuel-jr-jumps-route-to-snag-int-on-tua |access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Punturi |first=Jacob |date=December 16, 2025 |title=Watch: Steelers New CB Records First Interception |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/steelers/onsi/news/watch-pittsburgh-steelers-new-asante-samuel-jr-records-first-interception |access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=Pittsburgh Steelers On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 12, 2026, Samuel re-signed with the Steelers on a one-year, $4 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varley |first1=Teresa |title=Steelers sign Samuel |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-samuel |website=Steelers.com |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son of former NFL cornerback [[Asante Samuel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirshner |first=Alex |date=April 13, 2017 |title=Asante Samuel's son is already a top recruit, and he just picked FSU |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football/2017/4/13/15284786/asante-samuel-jr-cornerback-dad-signs-2018 |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=SBNation.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Asmar Bilal''' (born April 12, 1997) is an American [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]].

== Early life ==
Bilal played high school football at [[Ben Davis High School]] in [[Indianapolis]]. During his senior year, he earned 6A All-State honors and helped lead his team to a state championship while recording 155 tackles, 6 tackles for loss, 5 sacks, and an interception.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Peterson|first=Michael|date=2020-06-26|title=2020 UDFA Profile: LB Asmar Bilal|url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2020/6/26/21299203/chargers-news-nfl-asmar-bilal-udfa-2020|access-date=2020-09-23|website=Bolts From The Blue|language=en}}</ref> Bilal was also a participant in the [[U.S. Army All-American Game]] and was rated by [[ESPN]] as the 23rd best outside linebacker in the country.<ref name=":0" />

== College career ==
Bilal played college football at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]]. During his senior season, he had 79 total tackles with 10 for loss.<ref name="pandemic">{{Cite web|last=Star|first=Joel A. Erickson Indianapolis|title=Asmar Bilal one of the NFL Draft prospects the pandemic has hurt the worst|url=https://www.ndinsider.com/football/asmar-bilal-one-of-the-nfl-draft-prospects-the-pandemic-has-hurt-the-worst/article_817ff69d-35a7-585a-998f-da57ff9339a1.html|access-date=2020-09-23|website=Notre Dame Insider|language=en}}</ref> He finished his career with 45 game appearances and 174 total tackles.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Suarez|first=Brandon|date=|title=Irish On Tap 2020 NFL Draft Preview: Asmar Bilal|url=https://ontapsportsnet.com/2020/04/13/irish-on-tap-2020-nfl-draft-preview-asmar-bilal/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422154332/https://ontapsportsnet.com/2020/04/13/irish-on-tap-2020-nfl-draft-preview-asmar-bilal/ |archive-date=2020-04-22 |access-date=22 September 2020|website=On Tap Sports Net}}</ref> In 2019, he was named a [[Pro Football Focus]] All-American honorable mention.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Asmar Bilal Named A Pro Football Focus All-American|url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-asmar-bilal-named-pff-all-american|access-date=2020-09-23|website=SI.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
===Los Angeles Chargers===
Bilal went undrafted in the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He signed with the Los Angeles Chargers shortly after the draft.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-04-30|title=Notre Dame football: Los Angeles Chargers sign Asmar Bilal|url=https://slapthesign.com/2020/04/30/notre-dame-chargers-sign-asmar-bilal/|access-date=2020-09-23|website=Slap the Sign|language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020, and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=We've Trimmed Our Roster to 53|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/we-ve-reduced-our-roster-to-53|website=Chargers.com|date=September 5, 2020|accessdate=October 2, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Practice Squad Announced|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/practice-squad-2020|website=Chargers.com|date=September 6, 2020|accessdate=October 2, 2020}}</ref> He was promoted to the Chargers active roster on September 15 after an injury to starting linebacker [[Drue Tranquill]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Charean|date=2020-09-15|title=Chargers place Drue Tranquill on IR, promote Asmar Bilal|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/15/chargers-place-drue-tranquill-on-ir-promote-asmar-bilal/|access-date=2020-09-23|website=ProFootballTalk|language=en-US}}</ref> who started over Bilal at linebacker at Notre Dame during their time as teammates.<ref name=pandemic/> He was placed on injured reserve on September 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-announce-roster-moves-200926|website=Chargers.com|date=September 26, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on December 5, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chargers Announce Moves Prior to Sunday's Game |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-announce-moves-prior-to-dec-6-new-england |website=Chargers.com |date=December 5, 2020 |access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on December 12, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chargers Activate Justin Jackson from Injured Reserve |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-activate-justin-jackson-from-injured-reserve-dec-12 |website=Chargers.com |date=December 12, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On January 27, 2021, Bilal signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign Asmar Bilal to Reserve/Future contract|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/las-vegas-raiders-sign-asmar-bilal-to-reserve-future-contract|website=Raiders.com|date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders finalize initial 53-man roster for 2021 season|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/las-vegas-raiders-initial-53-man-roster-2021-nfl-season|website=Raiders.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on December 29, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign two linebackers, make COVID-19 transactions ahead of Week 17|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-two-linebackers-covid-19-transactions-nfl-week-17-colts-2021|website=Raiders.com|date=December 29, 2021}}</ref> He was released on January 11, 2022.

'''Artavis Pierce''' (born May 17, 1996) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[running back]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]].

==Professional career==
===Chicago Bears===
Pierce signed with the [[Chicago Bears]] as an undrafted free agent following the [[2020 NFL draft]] on April 28, 2020.<ref name="g249">{{cite web | last=Mayer | first=Chris | title=Auburndale High alum Pierce signs as UFA with Chicago Bears | website=Mid Florida Newspapers | date=2020-05-12 | url=https://www.midfloridanewspapers.com/winter_haven_sun/auburndale-high-alum-pierce-signs-as-ufa-with-chicago-bears/article_a5bf4600-9488-11ea-8ee0-0b4b078c10f3.html | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bears/news/oregon-running-back-artavis-pierce-among-bears-ufa-signings | access-date=2024-11-18}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on July 27, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=July 27, 2020 |title=Roster Move: Bears put Pierce on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-put-pierce-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=ChicagoBears.com |archive-date=July 29, 2020 later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=August 2, 2020 |title=Roster Moves: Bears activate Pierce, waive Maxwell |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-activate-pierce-waive-maxwell |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=ChicagoBears.com |archive-date=August 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804005627/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-activate-pierce-waive-maxwell |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on September 5, as day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 16 to practice squad The Bears promoted Pierce to the active roster on September 29.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arnold |first=Geoffrey C. |date=September 30, 2020 |title=Chicago Bears promote former Oregon State Beaver Artavis Pierce to the active roster |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2020/09/chicago-bears-promote-former-oregon-state-beaver-artavis-pierce-to-the-active-roster.html |access-date=November 20, 2020 |website=Oregon Live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiederer |first=Dan |date=September 30, 2020 |title=3 things we learned from Chicago Bears practice, including Artavis Pierce's opportunity at running back and Tashaun Gipson's experience with quarterback changes ===Cleveland Browns===
On January 5, 2022, Pierce was signed to the [[Cleveland Browns]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place Baker Mayfield, Sione Takitaki on injured reserve, make other roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-baker-mayfield-sione-takitaki-on-injured-reserve-make-other-roster- |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 5, 2022}}</ref>

=== DC Defenders ===
On November 17, 2022, Pierce was drafted by the [[DC Defenders]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=Rosters for all eight XFL teams: Full draft results and where Vic Beasley, Martavis Bryant landed |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/35053464/xfl-draft-results-2023-full-rosters-eight-teams-vic-beasley-martavis-bryant-picks |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve list by the team on March 14, 2023, and activated on May 16.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |website=XFL.com |access-date=May 16, 2023}}</ref> He was not part of the roster after the [[2024 UFL dispersal draft]] on January 15, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 UFL Team Rosters |url=https://www.theufl.com/rosters |website=TheUFL.com |access-date=January 21, 2024}}</ref>

===Edmonton Elks===
Pierce signed with the [[Edmonton Elks]] on March 21, 2025.<ref name="db">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/artavis-pierce-piercar01/transactions | title=Artavis Pierce | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=27 March 2025}}</ref> He was released on June 1, 2025.<ref name="db"/>

'''Asim Richards''' (born October 2, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina Tar Heels]].

==Early life==
Richards was born on October 2, 2000, in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asim Richards Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RichAs00.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref> He attended [[Haverford School]], where he played [[American football|football]] and [[basketball]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/123563365/philadelphia-daily-news/|newspaper=[[Philadelphia Daily News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=February 28, 2023|page=A25|title=Former Haverford School standout tackling big opportunity at combine|author=Jackson, Devin}} {{Open access}}</ref>

On the football team, he spent most of his time as a [[defensive end]] and [[tight end]]. As a [[Junior (education year)|junior]], he received second-team All-Inter-Ac honors at [[defensive end]].

As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], he started the final four games at [[offensive tackle]]. He received All-Inter-Ac League honors and a Mini Max award, given by the [[Maxwell Football Club]] to the standout players in eastern Pennsylvania.<ref name="auto1"/>

Richards finished his high school career with 133 tackles (31 for loss), 13 sacks, 3 forced fumbles and 3 fumble recoveries. He was ranked as a three-star prospect, the sixth-best recruit in the state and the 42nd-best tackle overall, he committed to play [[college football]] at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/asim-richards|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NFL Draft Profile: Asim Richards, Interior Offensive Linemen, North Carolina Tar Heels|date=December 19, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman in 2019, he appeared in 9 games, mostly in a backup role on the [[offensive line]] and on [[special teams]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/123563737/the-herald-sun/|newspaper=[[The Herald-Sun (Durham, North Carolina)|The Herald-Sun]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 17, 2020|page=B1|author=Fowler, Chapel|title=Left tackle Richards has Howell's back this season}} {{Open access}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2020, he was named the full starter at [[left tackle]], starting in all but one of the 12 games of the season.<ref name="auto1"/> He was part of an [[offensive line]] that included [[offensive guard]]s [[Joshua Ezeudu]] and [[Marcus McKethan]]. He also blocked for future [[NFL]] players [[Sam Howell]], [[Javonte Williams]] and [[Michael Carter (running back)|Michael Carter]].

As a junior in 2021, he started all 13 games at [[left tackle]] and blocked for future [[NFL]] running back [[Ty Chandler (American football)|Ty Chandler]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tarheelswire.usatoday.com/gallery/tar-heels-snapshot-profile-no-72-asim-richards/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Tar Heels Snapshot Profile: No. 72 Asim Richards|author=Adkins, Richard|date=July 17, 2022}}</ref>

As a senior in 2022, he started all 14 games at [[left tackle]] and was named third-team all-conference after allowing only three [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] on close to 1,050 snaps.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/asim-richards-g-north-carolina-nfl-draft-scouting-report-2023/|publisher=[[Pro Football Network]]|title=Asim Richards, G, North Carolina {{!}} NFL Draft Scouting Report|author=Garrett, Tommy|date=April 8, 2023}}</ref> He blocked for quarterback [[Drake Maye]], helping the offense place third in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in points per game, second in passing yards per game and total yards per game, and first in rushing.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://tarheelswire.usatoday.com/2023/01/30/unc-offensive-lineman-asim-richards-to-play-in-reeses-senior-bowl/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=UNC offensive lineman Asim Richards to play in Reese's Senior Bowl|author=Lasley, Alec|date=January 30, 2023}}</ref> Although Richards had one year of eligibility remaining, he opted to enter the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref name="auto"/> He finished with 38 career starts (37 at [[left tackle]], one at [[offensive guard|left guard]]), including 34 consecutive. He was invited to the [[2023 Senior Bowl]].<ref name="auto"/>

===Dallas Cowboys===
Richards was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fifth round (169th overall) of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-address-o-line-with-asim-richards|title=Cowboys Address O-Line With Asim Richards|last=Harris|first=Nick|website=dallascowboys.com|publisher=Dallas Cowboys|date=April 29, 2023|access-date=April 30, 2023}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in eight games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asim Richards 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RichAs00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 8 against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], saw action at left tackle early in the fourth quarter while Chuma Edoga was out with an ankle injury. He was declared inactive 9 contests and in the Wild Card playoff game against the [[Green Bay Packers]].

In 2024, he appeared in 13 games with one start at left tackle, while showing that he could also play the guard position. He missed four contests from Week 13 to Week 16 with an ankle injury. In Week 10 against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], he made his first start at left tackle in place of injured first round draft choice [[Tyler Guyton]]. He also saw significant playing time at left tackle in the season finale against the [[Washington Commanders]].

In 2025, he was expected to be the team's backup left tackle, but was passed on the depth chart during the preseason by second-year player [[Nathan Thomas (American football)|Nathan Thomas]].

===New Orleans Saints===
On August 26, 2025, Richards was traded to the [[New Orleans Saints]] along with a 2028 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{cite web | last=Walker | first=Patrik | title=Cowboys trade Asim Richards to Saints | website=Dallas Cowboys | date=2025-08-26 | url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-finalizing-asim-richards-trade-to-saints | access-date=2025-09-25}}</ref> He was acquired to be the team's backup swing tackle.

He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] and was selected in the fifth round (144th overall) of the [[2023 NFL draft]] by the [[New England Patriots]].

==Early life==
Mafi was born on October 20, 2000, and is of [[Tonga]]n descent.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/atonio-mafi|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NFL Draft Profile: Atonio ==College career==
Recruited to UCLA to play on the [[defensive line]], Mafi was measured at 411 pounds when he first entered the school.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/123625477/the-los-angeles-times/|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 28, 2022|page=D1, [https://newspapers.com/clip/123625656/the-los-angeles-times/ D7]|title=A leaner, meaner Mafi aims for a shot|author=Bolch, Ben}} {{Open access}}</ref> He had a jersey sized XXXXL, a size 50 waist, and 40% body fat.<ref name="auto1"/> One of his favorite meals at the time consisted of five beef patties with cheese, a double order of fries and a milkshake, which totaled 177 grams of fat and 3,240 calories, over 150% the daily recommended intake.<ref name="auto1"/> He was told he needed to lose weight to have a chance to play, and was able to drop to 390 by the time the season started.<ref name="auto1"/> Mafi won the starting job and was the only true [[freshman]] starting on the defensive line.<ref name="auto1"/> He appeared in 12 games on the year, starting nine, and recorded 16 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] at [[nose tackle]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite magazine |last=Connon, Sam |date=April 26, 2023 |title=NFL Draft Preview 2023: UCLA Football Offensive Guard Atonio Mafi |url=https://www.si.com/college/ucla/football/nfl-draft-preview-2023-ucla-football-offensive-guard-atonio-mafi |access-date=2024-07-27 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

Mafi slimmed down to 357 by the beginning of the 2019 season, and posted 28 tackles, including four {{abbr|TFLs|tackles-for-loss}}, one [[Quarterback sack|sack]] and one forced [[fumble]] while appearing in 12 games, five of which he started.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto2" /> He moved to the [[offensive line]] in 2020 and saw limited action in seven games as a reserve.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto2" /> The following year, Mafi played 12 games, three as a starter.<ref name="auto2" />

As Mafi entered his final year in 2022, he weighed at 377 pounds.<ref name="auto1"/> He was told he again needed to lose weight, with his coach saying, "If you lose the weight, you'll have a shot."<ref name="auto1"/> Mafi went on a diet and exercise plan and was eventually able to go down to 340 by the time the season started.<ref name="auto1"/> He ended up starting all 13 games and was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|all-conference]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]].<ref name="auto2" /> He finished his stint at UCLA with 56 games played, tying the school record.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kruse, Zach |date=April 13, 2023 |title=Packers host UCLA OL Atonio Mafi on official pre-draft visit |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/13/packers-host-ucla-ol-atonio-mafi-on-official-pre-draft-visit/ |access-date=2024-07-27 |work=[[USA Today]] |archive-date=April 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427164252/https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/13/packers-host-ucla-ol-atonio-mafi-on-official-pre-draft-visit/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Ashton Jeanty''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|dʒ|ɛ|n|t|i}} {{respell|JEN|tee}}; born December 2, 2003) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). An [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] playing [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]], he won the [[Maxwell Award|Maxwell]] and [[Doak Walker Award]]s and was the [[Heisman Trophy]] runner-up in 2024 after leading the [[Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS) in rushing yards and touchdowns. Jeanty was selected by the Raiders sixth overall in the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Jeanty was born on December 2, 2003, in [[Jacksonville, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Riley |first=Gavin |date=August 6, 2024 |title=Ashton Jeanty took an unconventional path to college football. Now, he's about to take it by storm |url=https://www.gavinriley.com/p/ashton-jeanty-took-an-unconventional |access-date=2024-09-29 |website=www.gavinriley.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kassim |first=Ehsan |date=September 21, 2024 |title=Who is Ashton Jeanty? What to know of Boise State football's Hesiman hopeful running back |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2024/09/21/ashton-jeanty-boise-state-broncos-football-running-back-who-stats-oregon/75240212007/ |access-date=2024-09-29 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> The son of Harry Jeanty, a [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]] [[Chief Petty Officer (United States)|chief petty officer]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Who Are Ashton Jeanty’s Parents? | website=The Playoffs | date=2025-04-25 | url=https://theplayoffs.news/en/who-are-ashton-jeanty-parents/ | access-date=2025-06-02}}</ref> He first played football at Great Bridge Middle School in [[Chesapeake, Virginia]]. As a high school freshman at [[Naples Middle/High School]], a school for [[Military brat (U.S. subculture)|military dependents]] near [[Naples]], [[Italy]], he was initially placed at quarterback before being moved to running back after two games. Playing against teams from other [[Department of Defense Education Activity|base schools]] throughout Europe, Jeanty ran for over 1,200 yards and scored 21 touchdowns in the team's six-game season.<ref name=Uggetti>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/41962943/boise-state-ashton-jeanty-dominant-running-back-heisman-2024 |title=Boise State's Ashton Jeanty has turned the ground game into a blockbuster |first=Paolo |last=Uggetti |website=ESPN.com |date=October 25, 2024 |access-date=October 25, 2024 |archive-date=December 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203185649/https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/41962943/boise-state-ashton-jeanty-dominant-running-back-heisman-2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>

After that season, Jeanty told his parents that he wanted to return to the U.S. to play high school football.<ref name=Uggetti/> He eventually attended [[Lone Star High School (Frisco, Texas)|Lone Star High School]] in [[Frisco, Texas]], where he rushed for 1,843 yards with 41 total touchdowns as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Riddle |first=Greg |date=2021-11-04 |title=How Frisco Lone Star's Ashton Jeanty could stand alongside Texas high school football legends |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/football/2021/11/04/how-frisco-lone-stars-ashton-jeanty-could-stand-alongside-texas-high-school-football-legends/ |access-date=2023-11-13 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref> He committed to [[Boise State University]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Riddle |first=Greg |date=2021-09-14 |title=Frisco Lone Star three-star running back/receiver Ashton Jeanty commits to Boise State |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/football/2021/09/13/frisco-lone-star-three-star-running-backreceiver-ashton-jeanty-commits-to-boise-state/ |access-date=2023-11-13 |website=Dallas News |language=en |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001093014/https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/football/2021/09/13/frisco-lone-star-three-star-running-backreceiver-ashton-jeanty-commits-to-boise-state/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2022 season===
As a true freshman at Boise State in 2022, Jeanty split playing time with [[George Holani]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Boise State Broncos Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boise-state/2022.html |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in all 14 games with two starts and finished the year with 821 yards on 156 carries and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaye |first=Jordan |date=October 4, 2022 |title=From Italy to Idaho, freshman Ashton Jeanty might be the next great BSU running back |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/from-italy-to-idaho-freshman-ashton-jeanty-might-be-the-next-great-bsu-running-back/article_b81a2762-444d-11ed-8d78-9f7d8493d428.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001093258/https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/from-italy-to-idaho-freshman-ashton-jeanty-might-be-the-next-great-bsu-running-back/article_b81a2762-444d-11ed-8d78-9f7d8493d428.html |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |access-date=September 23, 2023 |website=Idaho Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaye |first=Jordan |date=July 8, 2023 |title=Can Ashton Jeanty surpass George Holani as RB1? |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/can-ashton-jeanty-surpass-george-holani-as-rb1/article_67777434-1d02-11ee-b779-47cc6f898692.html |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=Idaho Press}}</ref> In the [[2022 Frisco Bowl]], he rushed for 178 yards and a touchdown in the 35–32 victory over North Texas.<ref>{{cite web | last=Counts | first=Ron | last2=Roberts | first2=Rachel | title=Boise State freshman sets Frisco Bowl record as Broncos rally to beat Mean Green | website=Idaho Statesman | date=2022-12-18 | url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article270151832.html | access-date=2025-04-30}}</ref>

[[File:Ashton Jeanty (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Jeanty with the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]] in 2023]]
Jeanty returned to Boise State in 2023 <ref name="e387">{{cite web | last=Roberts | first=Rachel | title=Powered by 'borderline surreal' moves, Boise State running back among nation's leaders | website=Idaho Statesman | date=2023-09-15 | url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article279374544.html | access-date=2024-10-01}}</ref>

During that season, Jeanty led the team in rushing yards with 1,347 and 14 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Boise State Broncos Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/boise-state/2023.html |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He also had 569 receiving yards, the second highest on the team and the most of any running back in the nation,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats/player/_/stat/receiving/season/2023|title=College Football Offense Receiving All Conferences Stat Leaders, 2023 Season|website=ESPN}}</ref> and five receiving touchdowns. === 2025 season ===
In his NFL debut in Week 1 against the [[New England Patriots]], Jeanty ran for 19 times, totaling 38 yards, scoring his first professional touchdown on a 3-yard rush.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Las Vegas Raiders vs. New England Patriots Live Score and Stats - September 7, 2025 Gametracker |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/boxscore/NFL_20250907_LV@NE/ |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> In Week 3 against the [[Washington Commanders]], Jeanty recorded 17 carries for 63 rushing yards. 
[[File:JG9 9756 (54841242599).jpg|thumb|Jeanty (middle) being [[tackled]] while playing against the Washington Commanders]]
In Week 4 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Jeanty had a career high in single-game touchdowns, scoring three. Two were on passes from quarterback [[Geno Smith]], accompanied by a 60-yard rushing touchdown. In the game, Jeanty compiled a total of 138 rushing yards on 21 carries and 17 receiving yards on 2 receptions, being named [[FedEx Ground NFL Player of the Week]] for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashton Jeanty voted Week 4 FedEx Ground Player of the Week |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/ashton-jeanty-voted-week-4-fedex-ground-player-of-the-week |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=Las Vegas Raiders |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-29 |title=Breaking Down Jeanty’s Stellar Performance |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/raiders/onsi/las-vegas-ashton-jeanty-chicago-bears-chip-kelly-geno-smith-pete-carroll |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=Las Vegas Raiders On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 6 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Jeanty recorded 23 carries for 75 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-12 |title=Raiders' Ashton Jeanty: Heavy involvement in win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/raiders-ashton-jeanty-heavy-involvement-in-win/ |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 16 on the road against the [[Houston Texans]], Jeanty had a notable performance, recording 188 total yards and two touchdowns, one a 60-yard catch, and the other a 51-yard run. Despite this, the Raiders lost narrowly, 23-21, against the NFL's top ranked defense that season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-22 |title=A rookie's incredible performance couldn't stop the Raiders' skid |url=https://apnews.com/article/raiders-jeanty-4191dbab18021ae8b92eaa7b64478681 |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Holder |first=Matt |date=2025-12-22 |title=Ashton Jeanty silences doubters against stout Houston Texans’ defense |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/las-vegas-raiders-scores-results/118051/las-vegas-raiders-houston-texans-score-ashton-jeanty |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Silver And Black Pride |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Jeanty finished his rookie season with 1,321 total scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns as he was named to the [[PFWA NFL All-Rookie Team]] for the [[2025 NFL season|2025 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-24 |title=Jeanty Rookie Stats |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/jeanty-rookie-stats |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashton Jeanty named to 2025 PFWA All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/ashton-jeanty-named-to-2025-pfwa-all-rookie-team |access-date=2026-06-24 |website=Las Vegas Raiders |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Ashton Gillotte''' ({{Respell|jill|-|OHT|-|ee}}''';''' born October 30, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]] and was selected by the Chiefs in the third round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Gillotte was born in [[Middletown, Ohio]] and moved to [[Florida]] when he was three years old after his parents were divorced.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Devin Gillotte - Football |url=https://gohatters.com/sports/football/roster/devin-gillotte/1694 |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Stetson University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He and his mother would settle in [[Boca Raton, Florida]] when he was in the sixth grade.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://cardinalsportszone.com/2020/07/05/perseverance-through-adversity-how-ashton-gillottes-journey-led-him-to-louisville/|title=Perseverance Through Adversity: How Ashton Gillotte's Journey Led Him To Louisville|website=cardinalsportszone.com|date=July 5, 2020|access-date=February 23, 2024}}</ref> Gillotte would attend [[Boca Raton Community High School]]. As a senior in 2020, he was the ''[[Sun Sentinel]]'''s Palm Beach County 8A-6A defensive player of the year after recording 55 tackles and 10 sacks in seven games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2021/01/16/palm-beach-8a-6a-defensive-player-of-the-year-ashton-gillotte-boca-raton-senior/|title=Palm Beach 8A-6A defensive player of the year: Ashton Gillotte, Boca Raton senior|date=16 January 2021 |publisher=South Florida Sun Sentinel|first=Adam|last=Lichtenstein}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Louisville]] to play college football.<ref>{{cite web | last=Aulbach | first=Lucas | title=Louisville football: Ashton Gillotte, 3-star 2021 prospect, commits | website=Courier-Journal | date=2020-05-18 | url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2020/05/18/louisville-football-ashton-gillotte-2021-defensive-end-commits/5211521002/ | access-date=2025-07-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/football/2020/05/18/boca-raton-highrsquos-ashton-gillotte-explains-louisville-commitment/41750861/|title=Boca Raton High's Ashton Gillotte explains Louisville commitment|publisher=The Palm Beach Post|date=18 May 2020|first=Phillip|last=Suitts}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Lichtenstein | first=Adam | title=Boca Raton defensive end Ashton Gillotte commits to Louisville over Duke, UCF and more | website=Sun Sentinel | date=2020-05-18 | url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2020/05/17/boca-raton-defensive-end-ashton-gillotte-commits-to-louisville-over-duke-ucf-and-more/ | access-date=2025-07-10}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Louisville in 2021, Gillotte played in 12 games and had 19 tackles and four sacks.<ref>{{cite web | last=Robinson | first=Cameron Teague | title=Louisville football's Ashton Gillotte's rise doesn't surprise to many | website=Courier-Journal | date=2021-08-17 | url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2021/08/17/louisville-footballs-ashton-gillottes-rise-doesnt-surprise-many/5537480001/ | access-date=2025-07-10}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2022, he started 12 games, recording 24 tackles and seven sacks. He returned to Louisville as a starter his junior year in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | last=Cubit | first=Alexis | title=Ashton Gillotte wants to grow as leader for Louisville football. His family is here to help | website=The Courier-Journal | url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2023/08/07/louisville-football-2023-ashton-gillotte-key-leader-defense/70456285007/ | language=en-US | access-date=2025-07-23}}</ref>
