'''Aston Rashaud Whiteside''' (born May 19, 1989) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Abilene Christian Wildcats football|Abilene Christian Wildcats]], where he was a four-time first-team [[Lone Star Conference]] (LSC) South selection and a three-time LSC South Defensive Lineman of the Year. After going undrafted in the [[2012 NFL draft]], he signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) but was waived before the start of the season. He then spent time on the [[practice squad]] of the [[Chicago Bears]] in 2012 and 2013, and the practice squad of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in 2013. Whiteside later played in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) from 2014 to 2017 for the [[Toronto Argonauts]], [[Ottawa Redblacks]], and [[Calgary Stampeders]]. He won the [[104th Grey Cup]] with the Redblacks in 2015. He was also an offseason member of the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] in 2017.

==Early life==
Aston Rashaud Whiteside was born on May 19, 1989, in [[Wichita County, Texas]].<ref name="pfa"/> He played both [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] and [[outside linebacker]] at [[Vernon High School (Vernon, Texas)|Vernon High School]] in [[Vernon, Texas]], from 2003 to 2006.<ref name="de">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/times-record-news/162548912/ | title=Move to DE pays off for ACU's Whiteside | work=[[Times Record News]] | date=November 17, 2009 | accessdate=8 January 2025 | author=Slavik, Coy |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |pages=1C, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/times-record-news/173242998/ 3C]}}</ref><ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/times-record-news/162550257/ | title=Whiteside hopes to be next in NFL line | work=[[Times Record News]] | date=July 29, 2011 | accessdate=8 January 2025 | author=Gholson, Nick|via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> He ran for 1,934 yards and 24 touchdown his [[Senior (education)|senior]] year in 2006, garnering first team all-district recognition while leading the team to a Class 3A Division II semifinals loss to [[Celina High School (Texas)|Celina High School]].<ref name="bio"/> He was named the [[most valuable player]] of the ''[[Times Record News]]'' Red River 22 team.<ref name="bio"/> Whiteside also played in the Texas High School Coaches Association all-star game as part of the North team, rushing five times for 15 yards in a 14–0 loss.<ref name="bio">{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/sports/football/roster/aston--whiteside/3535 | title=Aston Whiteside |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> He graduated from Vernon High in 2007.<ref name="bio"/>

==College career==
Whiteside played [[college football]] for the [[Abilene Christian Wildcats football|Abilene Christian Wildcats]] of [[NCAA Division II]] from 2008 to 2011 as a [[defensive end]].<ref name="bio"/><ref name="pfa"/> He initially joined the team as a [[linebacker]] but moved to defensive end his [[redshirt (sports)|redshirt]] year in 2007 after a series of injuries at the position.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="de"/> While at Abilene Christian, he played with his cousins [[Daryl Richardson]], [[Clyde Gates]], and [[Bernard Scott]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2012/4/28/FB_0428122844 | title=Richardson drafted by Rams; Whiteside signs with Cowboys |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=April 28, 2012 | accessdate=30 October 2024}}</ref>

Whiteside recorded 30 tackles, nine sacks, two forced fumbles, four fumble recoveries, three pass breakups, and one blocked kick in 2008.<ref name="bio"/> He returned two of his fumble recoveries for touchdowns.<ref name="bio"/> The Wildcats finished with a 10–0 record, which was the second [[perfect season]] in team history and the first [[1950 Abilene Christian Wildcats football team|since 1950]].<ref name="bio"/> He earned first-team all-[[Lone Star Conference]] (LSC) South Division, LSC South co-Defensive Lineman of the Year, LSC South Freshman of the Year, first-team [[Daktronics]] NCAA Division II all-Super Region 4, and Don Hansen's ''Football Gazette'' third team all-region honors that season.<ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2009/1/23/20634?path=general | title=More Wildcats honored |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=January 23, 2009 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref name="de"/> Whiteside totaled 9.5 sacks, 14.5 tackles for loss, and one pass breakup in 2009, garnering first-team All-LSC South, first-team [[All-American]], and first-team all-region accolades.<ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://lonestarconference.org/news/2009/11/12/091112_allconfSOUTH.aspx | title=Football: All-LSC South Division Awards announced |website=LoneStarConference.org | publisher=[[Lone Star Conference]] | date=November 12, 2009 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> His sack total that year was second in the LSC and first on the team.<ref name="bio"/>

Whiteside played in 12 games, starting 10, during the 2010 season, recording 28 tackles, seven sacks, five fumble recoveries, three blocked kicks, and one interception that he also returned for a touchdown.<ref name="bio"/> His sack total and 14.5 tackles for loss led the team in both categories.<ref name="bio"/> The Wildcats finished the regular season with an 11–0 record, the third perfect season in team history.<ref name="bio"/> He was named first-team all-LSC South, LSC South Defensive Lineman of the Year, ''Football Gazette'' third-team All-American, Daktronics all-Region IV, and Daktronics Region IV Defensive Player of the Year.<ref name="bio"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://lonestarconference.org/news/2010/11/17/FB_1117101842.aspx | title=Football: All-LSC South Division Awards announced |website=LoneStarConference.org | publisher=[[Lone Star Conference]] | date=November 17, 2010 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> He totaled 40 tackles and six sacks his senior year in 2011, earning first-team All-LSC South for the fourth consecutive year, LSC South Defensive Lineman of the Year for the third time, LSC South Defensive Player of the Year, and first-team [[American Football Coaches Association|AFCA]] All-American honors.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2011/12/1/FB_1201114747.aspx | title=Whiteside earns regional honor |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=December 1, 2011 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2011/12/15/FB_1215113446?path=general | title=Whiteside lauded as all-America |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=December 15, 2011 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://lonestarconference.org/news/2011/11/17/FB_1117115742.aspx | title=All-LSC Football Awards announced | website=LoneStarConference.org |publisher=[[Lone Star Conference]] | date=November 17, 2011 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> Whiteside finished his college career with the second most sacks in school history.<ref name="Pro day"/>

==Professional career==
On April 3, 2012, at Abilene Christian's [[Pro Day]], Whiteside ran drills at defensive end, [[defensive tackle]], outside linebacker, [[fullback (American football)|fullback]] and [[tight end]].<ref name="Pro day">{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2012/4/3/FB_0403120626.aspx | title=Richardson, Whiteside impress in front of 15 teams at ACU Pro Day |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=April 3, 2012 | accessdate=30 October 2024}}</ref> He recorded a 4.74 second [[40-yard dash]], a 33.5 inch [[vertical leap]], and 19 reps of 225 pounds in the [[bench press]].<ref name="Pro day"/>

After going undrafted in the [[2012 NFL draft]], Whiteside signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on May 4, 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/cowboys/2012/05/01/for-undrafted-abilene-christian-de-aston-whiteside-a-chance-is-all-he-needs/ | title=For undrafted Abilene Christian DE Aston Whiteside, a chance is all he needs | work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] | date=Apr 30, 2012 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/> He grew up a Cowboys fan.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/times-record-news/162549712/ | title=Transition Game | work=[[Times Record News]] | date=May 7, 2012 | accessdate=8 January 2025 | author=Eatman, Nick | pages=6D|via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> He was moved to [[inside linebacker]] while with the Cowboys, and was later waived on August 5, 2012.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/times-record-news/162549631/ | title=Transition Game | work=[[Times Record News]] | date=May 7, 2012 | accessdate=8 January 2025 | author=Eatman, Nick | pages=1D}}</ref><ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/w/whit17060.html | title=Aston Whiteside | work=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref>

Whiteside signed with the [[Chicago Bears]] of the NFL as a defensive end on August 11, 2012.<ref name="transactions"/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-north-platte-telegraph/162550088/ | title=Transactions | work=[[The North Platte Telegraph]] | date=August 12, 2012 | accessdate=8 January 2025|via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> He was waived on August 31 and signed to the team's practice squad on September 2.<ref name="transactions"/> In October 2012, as part of a prank by Bears veterans, Whiteside and fellow rookie [[Shea McClellin]] were given a fake $38,091.91 dinner bill.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/nfl/story/_/id/8487024/chicago-bears-israel-idonije-pranks-shea-mcclellin-fake-dinner-bill | title=Israel Idonije pranks rookies | publisher=[[ESPN.com]] | date=October 10, 2012 | accessdate=27 May 2025 | author=Dickerson, Jeff}}</ref> Whiteside was waived again on October 16, and re-signed to the practice squad on November 28.<ref name="transactions"/> Whiteside signed a futures contract with the Bears on December 30, 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.chicagobears.com/team/transactions/2012 | title=TRANSACTIONS | publisher=[[Chicago Bears]] | accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> He was waived by the Bears on August 30, 2013, and signed to the practice squad on September 2.<ref name="transactions"/> He was waived by the Bears for the last time on October 8, 2013.<ref name="transactions"/>

Whiteside was signed to the practice squad of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the NFL on November 11, 2013.<ref name="transactions"/> He was waived on December 3, 2013.<ref name="transactions"/>

Whiteside signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on February 24, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.argonauts.ca/page/2014-transactions | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140604101609/http://www.argonauts.ca/page/2014-transactions | url-status=dead | archive-date=2014-06-04 | title=2014 Transactions | publisher=[[Toronto Argonauts]] | accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> He dressed in 15 games, starting 14, for the Argonauts during the 2014 season.<ref name="pfa"/> He also had two stints on the injured list.<ref name="cfl">{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/aston-whiteside/159239/#transactions | title=Aston Whiteside | website=CFL.ca |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]| accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> On October 8, 2014, he was fined by the CFL for "an illegal and dangerous hit on a quarterback in which he led with his helmet".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/cfl-fines-eskimos-rb-lawrence-and-argos-dl-whiteside-1.102344 | title=CFL fines Eskimos RB Lawrence and Argos DL Whiteside | website=[[The Sports Network|TSN.ca]] | date=October 8, 2014 | accessdate=30 October 2024}}</ref> Overall, he recorded 17 defensive tackles, two sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, and one pass breakup in 2014.<ref name="pfa"/> Whiteside was released by the Argonauts on June 21, 2015.<ref name="cfl"/>

Whiteside was signed to the practice roster of the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the CFL on July 20, 2015.<ref name="cfl"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://ottawasun.com/2015/08/06/aston-whiteside-makes-great-first-impression-with-redblacks | title=Aston Whiteside makes great first impression with RedBlacks | work=[[Ottawa Sun]] | date=August 6, 2015 | accessdate=4 September 2024 | author=Hofley, Chris}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on July 23.<ref name="cfl"/> He was ranked second on the CFL Top Performers of the Week for Week 5 after accumulating two tackles, two sacks, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery in a 29–26 overtime win over the [[Calgary Stampeders]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://acusports.com/news/2015/7/29/FB_0729155504 | title=Whiteside named a CFL Shaw Top Performer for Week 5 |website=ACUsports.com | publisher=[[Abilene Christian University]] | date=July 29, 2015 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://press.cfl.ca/shaw-cfl-top-performers-of-the-week-week-6 | title=SHAW CFL TOP PERFORMERS OF THE WEEK - WEEK 6 | website=CFL.ca |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]| accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> Whiteside suffered a season-ending knee injury on August 30 against the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ottawasun.com/2015/09/01/redblacks-de-aston-whiteside-to-miss-rest-of-season | title=RedBlacks' DE Aston Whiteside to miss rest of season | work=[[Ottawa Sun]] | date=September 2, 2015 | accessdate=30 October 2024 | author=Baines, Tim}}</ref><ref name="Injury">{{cite web | url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/cfl-55-yard-line/ottawa-redblacks-win-whilst-losing-aston-whiteside--their-sacks-leader-223119785.html | title=Ottawa Redblacks win whilst losing Aston Whiteside, their sacks leader | publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] | date=August 30, 2015 | accessdate=30 October 2024 | author=Sager, Neate}}</ref> He was leading the team with seven sacks at the time of his injury.<ref name="Injury"/> Overall, he played in five games, all starts, for the Redblacks during the 2015 season, totaling 13 defensive tackles, seven sacks, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery.<ref name="pfa"/> He was transferred to the retired list on April 25, 2016.<ref name="cfl"/> However, he was later transferred back to active status on May 29.<ref name="cfl"/> Whiteside appeared in 11 games, all starts, in 2016, accumulating 13 defensive tackles, one special teams tackle, three sacks, two forced fumbles, and one pass breakup.<ref name="pfa"/> He also had several stints on the injured list that year.<ref name="cfl"/> On November 27, 2016, the Redblacks won the [[104th Grey Cup]] against the [[Calgary Stampeders]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/football/cfl/ottawa-redblacks-pull-off-huge-upset-defeat-calgary-stampeders-in-wild-overtime-win-to-claim-2016-grey-cup | title=Ottawa Redblacks pull off wild upset, defeat Calgary Stampeders in overtime to claim 2016 Grey Cup | work=[[National Post]] | date=November 28, 2016 | accessdate=27 May 2025}}</ref> He became a free agent after the 2016 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/big-names-among-list-of-pending-cfl-s-free-agents-1.620485 | title=Big names among list of pending CFL's free agents | website=[[TSN.ca]] | date=November 30, 2016 | accessdate=4 September 2024 | author=Lawless, Gary}}</ref>

Whiteside signed with the CFL's [[Edmonton Eskimos]] on February 16, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2017/02/16/esks-sign-former-redblacks-van-whiteside/ | title=Esks sign former REDBLACKS Van, Whiteside | website=CFL.ca |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] | date=February 16, 2017 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref> On May 28, he was transferred to the suspended list after having passport issues.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2017/06/14/checking-law-lost-season/ | title=Checking Down: Law could be lost for season | website=CFL.ca |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] | date=June 14, 2017 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref><ref name="cfl"/> He was released by the Eskimos on June 13, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2017/06/13/esks-release-international-dl-aston-whiteside/ | title=Esks release international DL Aston Whiteside | website=CFL.ca |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] | date=June 13, 2017 | accessdate=4 September 2024}}</ref>

Whiteside was signed to the practice roster of the Calgary Stampeders of the CFL on July 3, 2017.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://calgaryherald.com/sports/football/calgary-stampeders-davaris-daniels-could-be-eyeing-quick-return | title=Calgary Stampeders' DaVaris Daniels could be eyeing quick return | work=[[Calgary Herald]] | date=July 3, 2017 | accessdate=27 May 2025 | author=Austin, Daniel}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on July 6 after [[Charleston Hughes]] suffered an injury.<ref name="cfl"/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/calgary-herald/162550734/ | title=Stamps' defence resembling MASH unit | work=[[Calgary Herald]] | date=July 8, 2017 | accessdate=8 January 2025 | author=Austin, Daniel|via=[[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> He played in one game for the Stampeders in 2017, recording one defensive tackle, before being transferred to the injured list on July 13.<ref name="pfa"/><ref name="cfl"/> Whiteside was released by the Stampeders on August 30, 2017.<ref name="cfl"/>

'''Arvell Reese''' (born August 30, 2005) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Reese played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]], winning the [[2025 College Football Playoff National Championship|2024 national championship]] before being selected fifth overall by the Giants in the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Reese was born on August 30, 2005 in [[Cleveland, Ohio]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mallick |first=Ananya |date=2026-04-08 |title=Where Is Arvell Reese From? All You Need to Know About The Ohio State LB's Ethnicity |url=https://www.totalprosports.com/ncaa/ohio-state-university/arvell-reese-from-ethnicity/ |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=TotalProSports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arvell Reese LB Ohio State |url=https://www.nfldraftbuzz.com/Player/Arvell-Reese-LB-OhioState |website=nfldraftbuzz.com |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Glenville High School]] in Cleveland's [[Glenville, Cleveland|Glenville]] neighborhood and was rated as a four-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Means |first1=Stephen |title=Glenville once saved Arvell Reese's life; now he's returning the favor by reviving the Ohio State pipeline |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2023/02/glenville-once-saved-arvell-reeses-life-now-hes-returning-the-favor-by-reviving-the-ohio-state-pipeline.html |website=Cleveland.com |date=6 February 2023 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
As a [[freshman]] in 2023, Reese only appeared in six games due to a concussion, recording no statistics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arvell Reese 2023 Game Logs |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/arvell-reese-1/gamelog/2023/ |website=Sports Reference |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Joey |title=How Arvell Reese has moved up in Ohio State football linebacker rotation |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/football/2024/09/20/ohio-state-football-arvell-reese-2024-roster-defense-starters/75297173007/ |website=The Columbus Dispatch |date=20 September 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> In the 2024 season opener, he notched four tackles with one being for a loss in a win over [[2024 Akron Zips football team|Akron]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Teague Robinson |first1=Cameron |title=How good can Ohio State's defense be? Arvell Reese's growth illustrates staggering depth |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5781824/2024/09/20/arvell-reese-ohio-state-defense-depth-chart/ |website=The Athletic |date=20 September 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> In week 9, Reese recorded two tackles but was ejected due to a questionable targeting call late in the fourth quarter against [[2024 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team|Nebraska]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schmidt |first1=Lori |title=Arvell Reese ejected for targeting in Ohio State vs Nebraska football game |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/football/2024/10/26/ohio-state-football-arvell-reese-targeting-nebraska-ejected/75649039007/ |website=The Columbus Dispatch |date=26 October 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Krajisnik |first1=Stefan |title=Will Arvell Reese be suspended vs. Penn State? Here's how Ohio State football's appeal went |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2024/10/will-arvell-reese-be-suspended-vs-penn-state-heres-how-ohio-state-footballs-appeal-went.html |website=Cleveland.com |date=28 October 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> The call was later overturned on appeal, lifting Reese's suspension for the Buckeyes' matchup versus [[2024 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|Penn State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rabinowitz |first1=Bill |title=Big Ten rules Ohio State LB Arvell Reese not guilty of targeting, lifts suspension |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/football/2024/10/28/big-ten-lifts-targeting-suspension-of-ohio-states-arvell-reese/75899515007/ |website=The Columbus Dispatch |date=28 October 2024 |access-date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> As of the 2025 season, Reese has become a highly touted linebacker for the [[2026 NFL Draft]], and has become one of the best linebackers in the country. On January 8, 2026, Reese declared for the draft.<ref>{{cite web | last=Trotter | first=Jake |author-link=Jake Trotter| title=Ohio State LB Arvell Reese, likely top-5 pick, enters NFL draft | website=ESPN.com | date=2026-01-08 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/47552889/ohio-state-lb-arvell-reese-likely-top-5-pick-enters-nfl-draft | access-date=2026-04-24}}</ref>

Reese was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the first round with the fifth overall pick of the [[2026 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=April 23, 2026 |title=Giants select Ohio State LB Arvell Reese at No. 5 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/giants-select-ohio-state-edge-rusher-arvell-reese-at-no-5 |access-date=May 18, 2026 |publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}}</ref> On May 29, 2026, he signed a four-year, $47.8 million contract with the Giants that included a $31.2 million signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web| last=Murphy | first=Patrick | date=May 29, 2026 | title= Former Ohio State LB Arvell Reese signs rookie contract with New York Giants | website=247Sports | url= https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/article/former-ohio-state-football-lb-arvell-reese-signs-rookie-contract-with-new-york-giants-286874336/ | access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref>
